Unassigned programs

1. Customer add, update and menudraft · online and scheduled job · 13 requirements · 10 rules · 14 criteria · 9 screens · 1 gap

Lets customer service staff register new customers and change the details of existing ones from the customer screen; new customers always get their number from the system, never from the user. It must always normalise the postcode to upper case and record the highest customer number issued after every successful add, and it must roll back a failed add so no partial customer is left behind.

As a customer service user, I want to add new customers and update existing customer details from the customer screen, so that customer records are created with a system-assigned number and kept current.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data, updates_records. rec/unassigned#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001business ruleWhen the user chooses option '2' on the customer screen, the system shall send an add-customer request ('01ACUS') to the customer add program (LGACUS01) with customer number 0 and the entered details, after turning any null characters into spaces and the postcode into upper case.AC-11
REQ-F-002formattingWhen the add-customer request returns code 0, the system shall update the customer-number control queue, show the assigned customer number, clear the option field and display 'New Customer Inserted'.AC-01
REQ-F-003side effectWhen a new customer has been added successfully, the system shall lock the control queue 'GENACNTL', find its 'HIGH CUSTOMER' entry, rewrite that entry as 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' followed by the new customer number, leave the 'LOW CUSTOMER=' entry unchanged and then release the lock.AC-12
REQ-F-004side effectIf the control queue 'GENACNTL' does not exist or has no 'HIGH CUSTOMER' entry, then the system shall write three entries to it: '**** GENAPP CNTL', 'LOW CUSTOMER=' and 'HIGH CUSTOMER=', each with the new customer number.AC-13
REQ-F-005error handlingIf the add-customer request returns a code greater than 0, then the system shall roll back the unit of work, display 'Error Adding Customer' and clear the screen data.AC-02
REQ-F-006business ruleWhen the user chooses option '4', the system shall first look up the customer ('01ICUS', LGICUS01) and display the current details.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-007business ruleIf the customer lookup for option '4' returns a code greater than 0, then the system shall display 'No data was returned.' and stop.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-008business ruleWhen the user changes the displayed customer details and presses Enter, the system shall send an update request ('01UCUS') to the customer update program (LGUCUS01) with the customer number and all fields from the screen, after turning null characters into spaces and the postcode into upper case.AC-14
REQ-F-009error handlingWhen the customer update returns code 0, the system shall display 'Customer details updated'.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-010error handlingIf the customer update returns a code greater than 0, then the system shall display 'Error Updating Customer' and clear the screen data, without a rollback.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-011business ruleIf the user enters an option other than '1' (inquire), '2' (add) or '4' (update), including blank or '3', then the system shall call no back-end program, display 'Please enter a valid option', place the cursor on the option field and wait for the next input under transaction 'SSC1'.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-012formattingWhen the user presses PF3 on the customer screen, the system shall display 'Transaction ended' and end the conversation.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-013formattingWhen the user presses CLEAR on the customer screen, the system shall redisplay an empty customer screen and continue under 'SSC1'.AC-09, AC-10

Open questions

  • SME-081 Is the recorded low/high customer number range the official range that other processes (such as workload generators) rely on, and should the high value only ever go up? (Application owner)
  • SME-082 New customer registration assigns the customer number automatically and normalises the postcode. Is this rule critical to the business, or costly if it were wrong, so that it must be preserved exactly? (Customer services business owner)
  • DEF-052 Is this intended? When the queue exists but has no 'HIGH CUSTOMER' entry, the header and both LOW and HIGH entries are appended after the existing items, which can leave a second header and LOW entry in the queue. The HIGH entry is also overwritten with whatever number was just assigned, without checking that it is higher than the current one. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-061 Is this intended? The update takes the customer number from the screen after the edit, not the number that was looked up, so a user who changes the customer number field updates a different customer. The task also holds the terminal open (conversationally) while the user edits. (Subject-matter expert)

2. Motor policy inquire, add, delete and updatedraft · online and scheduled job · 15 requirements · 12 rules · 14 criteria · 9 screens

Lets policy administrators look up, add, delete and update a customer's motor policy: vehicle details, dates, premium and accident count. A motor policy can only be added for a customer who already exists ('Customer does not exist' otherwise), and a failed add or delete must be rolled back. Policies added or updated on this screen always carry no payment and no broker, so an update overwrites any payment and broker details stored before.

As a policy administrator, I want to inquire on, add, delete and update motor policies from the motor policy screen, so that motor cover held for customers is kept correct.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/unassigned#2

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-014business ruleThe system shall offer on the motor policy screen (transaction SSP1) option '1' Inquire, '2' Add, '3' Delete and '4' Update.AC-01
REQ-F-015business ruleIf any other option is entered on the motor policy screen, then the system shall show 'Please enter a valid option' with the cursor on the option field.AC-01
REQ-F-016formattingWhen option '1' is entered, the system shall request the motor policy (request 01IMOT to LGIPOL01) for the entered customer and policy number and display issue date, expiry date, make, model, value, registration, colour, engine CC, manufacture date, premium and accident count.AC-02
REQ-F-017error handlingIf the motor policy inquiry returns a non-zero return code, then the system shall show 'No data was returned.' and clear the screen and request data for the next entry.AC-03
REQ-F-018business ruleWhen option '2' is entered on the motor policy screen, the system shall add a motor policy (request 01AMOT to LGAPOL01) from the entered customer number, dates and vehicle details, always with payment 0, broker id 0 and a blank broker reference.AC-04
REQ-F-019formattingWhen the motor policy add succeeds, the system shall show the customer number, the newly assigned policy number and 'New Motor Policy Inserted', and clear the option.AC-05
REQ-F-020error handlingIf the motor policy add returns a non-zero code, then the system shall roll back the unit of work and show 'Customer does not exist' for code 70 (customer not on file) or 'Error Adding Motor Policy' for any other code.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-021business ruleWhen option '3' is entered on the motor policy screen, the system shall delete the motor policy (request 01DMOT to LGDPOL01) for the entered customer and policy number.AC-08
REQ-F-022formattingWhen the motor policy delete succeeds, the system shall show 'Motor Policy Deleted' with the dates, make, model, value, registration, colour, CC and manufacture date blanked, leaving premium, accident count and the option not cleared.AC-09
REQ-F-023error handlingIf the motor policy delete returns a non-zero code, then the system shall roll back the unit of work and show 'Error Deleting Motor Policy'.AC-10
REQ-F-024business ruleWhen option '4' is entered on the motor policy screen, the system shall first display the current motor policy (request 01IMOT) and wait for the user to edit and resubmit it.AC-11
REQ-F-025business ruleIf the motor policy cannot be read for option '4', then the system shall show 'No data was returned.'.AC-11
REQ-F-026business ruleWhen the user resubmits the edited motor policy, the system shall send the update (request 01UMOT to LGUPOL01) with the screen values and payment 0, broker id 0 and a blank broker reference, replacing any stored payment and broker details.AC-12
REQ-F-027error handlingWhen the motor policy update succeeds, the system shall show 'Motor Policy Updated' and clear the option.AC-13, AC-14
REQ-F-028error handlingIf the motor policy update returns a non-zero code, then the system shall show 'Error Updating Motor Policy' without a rollback.AC-13, AC-14

Open questions

  • SME-083 Adding a motor policy requires an existing customer and always sets payment to 0 and broker id and broker reference to blank. Is this rule critical to the business, or costly if it were wrong, so that it must be preserved exactly? (Underwriting business owner)
  • SME-084 When a motor policy is updated, the payment, broker id and broker reference are reset to zero. Are these values actually saved on update, is resetting them intended, and should a failed update be rolled back? (Underwriting business owner)
  • DEF-062 Is this intended? After a successful motor delete the premium and accident count stay on screen and the option is not cleared (the house screen clears its option), and the screen is sent twice in a row. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

3. Endowment (life) policy inquire, add, delete and updatedraft · online and scheduled job · 16 requirements · 15 rules · 21 criteria · 9 screens · 2 gaps

Lets policy administrators look up, add, delete and update a customer's endowment (life) policy: fund, term, sum assured, life assured and the with-profits, managed-fund and equities indicators. Policies entered here always carry payment 0 and no broker, a failed add must be rolled back, and every failure must clear the screen ready for the next attempt. In the legacy screen the add-failure message ('Customer does not exist' or 'Error Adding Life Policy') goes to the motor screen's message field, so the user never sees it; the team must decide whether to keep that behaviour on purpose.

As a policy administrator, I want to inquire on, add, delete and update endowment (life) policies from the endowment policy screen, so that customers' life cover is recorded correctly.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/unassigned#3

REQ-F-030business ruleIf the operator presses Enter on the endowment policy screen with an option other than '1', '2', '3' or '4', then the system shall call no back-end program, show 'Please enter a valid option' with the cursor on the option field, and wait for the next input under transaction SSP2.AC-02, AC-03

Open questions

  • SME-085 When a policy is updated from a terminal, its broker id, broker reference and payment are reset to zero/blank. Is that intended, or should the stored values be kept? (Underwriting business owner)
  • DEF-058 Is this intended? The add-failure messages are written to the motor policy map's message field (ERP1FLDO) instead of the endowment map's (ERP2FLDO), so an operator never sees 'Customer does not exist' or 'Error Adding Life Policy' on the endowment screen. It looks like a copy from LGTESTP1; every other error path in this program uses ERP2FLDO. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-063 Is this intended? For the update, the customer number is re-read from the screen but the policy number is not; the policy number left from the inquiry is used, so a policy number the operator changes on the screen is ignored. The update failure path also does not roll back, although add and delete do. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

None.

4. House policy add, delete and updatedraft · online and scheduled job · 9 requirements · 8 rules · 10 criteria · 3 screens · 2 gaps

Lets policy administrators add, delete and update a customer's house policy: property type, bedrooms, value, house name, number and postcode. Policies entered here always carry payment 0 and no broker, replacing whatever was stored before, and a failed add or delete must be rolled back. In the legacy screen a failed add resets the screen without showing 'Customer does not exist' or 'Error Adding House Policy'; the team must decide whether to keep that.

As a policy administrator, I want to add, delete and update house policies from the house policy screen, so that customers' property cover is recorded correctly.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, updates_records. rec/unassigned#4

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-045business ruleWhen option '2' is entered on the house policy screen, the system shall add a house policy (request 01AHOU to LGAPOL01) from the entered customer number, dates, property type, bedrooms, value, house name, house number and postcode, with payment 0, broker id 0 and a blank broker reference.AC-01, AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-046formattingWhen the house policy add succeeds, the system shall show the customer number, the newly assigned policy number and 'New House Policy Inserted', and clear the option.AC-04
REQ-F-047error handlingIf the house policy add returns a non-zero code, then the system shall roll back the unit of work and reset the screen, without the intended message 'Customer does not exist' (code 70) or 'Error Adding House Policy' being shown on the house screen.AC-05
REQ-F-048business ruleWhen option '3' is entered on the house policy screen (transaction SSP3), the system shall delete the house policy (request 01DHOU to LGDPOL01) and on success blank the dates and property details, clear the option and show 'House Policy Deleted'.AC-06
REQ-F-049error handlingIf the house policy delete returns a non-zero code, then the system shall roll back the unit of work, show 'Error Deleting House Policy' and reset the screen and request data.AC-07
REQ-F-050business ruleWhen option '4' is entered on the house policy screen, the system shall first display the current house policy (request 01IHOU), then send the edited values as an update (request 01UHOU to LGUPOL01) with payment 0, broker id 0 and a blank broker reference, whatever values the policy held before.AC-02, AC-03, AC-08
REQ-F-051business ruleIf the current house policy cannot be read for option '4', then the system shall show 'No data was returned.'.AC-08
REQ-F-052error handlingWhen the house policy update succeeds, the system shall show 'House Policy Updated' and clear the option.AC-09, AC-10
REQ-F-053error handlingIf the house policy update returns a non-zero code, then the system shall show 'Error Updating House Policy' and reset the screen, without a rollback.AC-09, AC-10

5. Commercial property policy inquire, add and deletedraft · online and scheduled job · 17 requirements · 15 rules · 19 criteria · 9 screens · 1 gap

Lets policy administrators find, add and delete commercial property policies, including location, property type, the fire, crime, flood and weather perils and premiums, status and reject reason. A search uses the most specific key given: customer and policy number first, then policy number alone, then customer number alone, then postcode. A policy can only be added for an existing customer, and a failed add or delete must be rolled back.

As a policy administrator, I want to find, add and delete commercial property policies from the commercial policy screen, so that commercial cover, perils and premiums for customers are recorded correctly.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/unassigned#5

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-054formattingWhen the commercial policy transaction starts with no prior conversation data, the system shall show a fresh form with customer and policy numbers '0000000000' and empty peril, premium and status fields.AC-01
REQ-F-055business ruleIf the user enters any option other than '1', '2' or '3' on the Commercial Policy menu, including a blank option, then the system shall show 'Please enter a valid option', put the cursor on the option field, and call no back-end service.AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-056business ruleWhen option '1' is entered with both a customer number and a policy number (neither blank nor zero), the system shall ask the policy inquiry service (LGIPOL01) for that customer's policy using request type '01ICOM'.AC-04
REQ-F-057business ruleWhen option '1' is entered with a policy number but no customer number, the system shall search by policy number using request type '02ICOM'.AC-05
REQ-F-058business ruleWhen option '1' is entered with a customer number but no policy number, the system shall search by customer number using request type '03ICOM'.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-059business ruleWhen option '1' is entered with neither a customer number nor a policy number but with a postcode, the system shall search by postcode using request type '05ICOM'.AC-06, AC-07
REQ-F-060formattingWhen the policy inquiry succeeds, the system shall show the policy number, customer number, issue and expiry dates, address, postcode, latitude, longitude, customer name, property type, the fire, crime, flood and weather peril and premium values, status and reject reason.AC-08
REQ-F-061error handlingIf the policy inquiry service returns a non-zero code, then the system shall show 'No data was returned.' and clear the screen data for the next entry.AC-09
REQ-F-062business ruleWhen option '2' is entered, the system shall send the customer number, issue and expiry dates, address, postcode, latitude, longitude, customer name, property type, peril and premium values, status and reject reason to the add-policy service (LGAPOL01) as request '01ACOM'.AC-10
REQ-F-063formattingWhen the add-policy service returns code 0, the system shall show the customer number and the newly assigned policy number, clear the option field and show 'New Commercial Policy Inserted'.AC-11
REQ-F-064error handlingIf the add-policy service returns a non-zero code, then the system shall roll back the work and show 'Customer does not exist' if the code is 70, or 'Error Adding Commercial Policy' for any other code.AC-12, AC-13
REQ-F-065business ruleWhen option '3' is entered, the system shall ask the delete-policy service (LGDPOL01) to delete the given customer's policy using request '01DCOM'.AC-14
REQ-F-066formattingWhen the commercial policy delete succeeds (code 0), the system shall blank the expiry date, address, postcode, latitude, longitude, customer name, property type, peril and premium values, status and reject reason, clear the option field and show 'Commercial Policy Deleted'.AC-15
REQ-F-067error handlingIf the delete-policy service returns a code above 0, then the system shall roll back the work and show 'Error Deleting Commercial Policy'.AC-16
REQ-N-001design noteWhen an option has been processed, the system shall return control so the next Enter continues under transaction 'SSP4'.AC-17
REQ-F-068formattingWhen the user presses PF3, or the commercial policy screen is received with no data, the system shall show 'Transaction ended' and end the session.AC-18, AC-19
REQ-F-069formattingWhen the user presses Clear on the commercial policy screen, the system shall redisplay an empty form and continue under 'SSP4'.AC-18, AC-19

Design notes

  • After each option has been processed, the commercial policy screen stays open with its current values, so the user's next submission is handled by the same commercial policy screen and starts the next action. This is ordinary screen navigation in the new application: it needs no transaction code, only a way to keep the user on the commercial policy page between actions until they leave it (PF3 / exit) or clear it. Application Deployment Lifecycle Management

Application Deployment and Policy Lifecycle Management

1. Load customer and policy data storesdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 2 rules · 4 criteria

Fills the new customer store and policy store with every record from the supplied customer and policy input files, so the online application starts with its existing records already in place. It is run by application administrators as part of setting up an environment. Each load runs only if its store was created successfully, and it must copy every record, with none dropped or changed.

As an application administrator, I want the new customer and policy data stores filled from the supplied input data sets once they are defined, so that the online application starts with its customer and policy records in place.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#1

REQ-F-002design noteIf the step that defines the policy data store (DEFINE2) ends with a return code above 7, then the system shall skip the load of the policy data store.AC-01, AC-02

Open questions

  • SME-001 The two data loads are identified only by legacy labels. Which data stores are the input and the target for the first load and for the second load? (Application data owner)
  • SME-002 Each load copies every record into its target store. Is the target store empty before the load, or are existing records replaced, merged, or rejected as duplicates? (Application data owner)
  • SME-003 If a load stops partway through, should a rerun start again from the beginning, and must the target store be cleared first? (Batch operations)

Design notes

  • A one-time bulk import step in the environment set-up pipeline. It copies every record from the supplied policy extract into the policy store and depends on the step that creates the store: run the import when that step succeeded (severity 7 or less) or was skipped, and skip it when that step failed with a severity above 7. Report how many records were read and how many were written so the load can be reconciled. Load second data store from input
  • The same guarded bulk import for customers. Copy every record from the supplied customer extract into the customer store, but only when the step that creates the store succeeded (severity 7 or less) or did not run. Skip the import when that step failed with a severity above 7. Report the record counts. Load first data store from input
2. Define online files and transactionsdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 9 rules · 13 criteria

Declares the customer and policy record stores and the eight insurance entry points (customer and policy menus, set-up, and the customer and policy counters), so users can reach the insurance functions. It is for the administrators who deploy the application. It must never let online functions delete customer records: policies can be added, read, browsed, updated and deleted, but customers can only be added, read, browsed and updated.

As an application administrator, I want the online region to define the customer and policy files and the insurance transactions, so that users can reach the insurance programs and records can be maintained online with the right permissions.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#2

Open questions

  • SME-004 Users can start these functions: the customer menu, the motor, life, house and commercial policy menus, setup, and two inquiry functions. Which transaction code starts each function? (Application owner)
  • SME-005 Every transaction is set up so its working data can sit anywhere in memory and runs under the user key. These are settings of the old platform. Does the new platform need anything equivalent, or can these settings be dropped? (Platform architecture)
  • SME-006 Customer records are 82 bytes long and policy records are 64 bytes long. Is the new system required to keep these record lengths, or are they only a detail of how the old system stores the data? (Data architecture)
  • SME-007 Customer keys are 10 bytes long and policy keys are 21 bytes long. Must the new system keep these lengths as rules for customer and policy identifiers, or are they only a storage detail? (Data architecture)
  • SME-008 Customer records cannot be deleted through the online system. Does this mean customer records must never be deleted at all, or only that they must not be deleted online? (Insurance business owner)
  • DEF-034 Is this intended? CDEF123 adds group GENADORT to list DORLIST, but no GENADORT group is deleted or defined in this job (CDEF122 does not add it); the list entry points at a group that may not exist. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Declare the policy store in deployment configuration. It holds 64-character records under a 21-character key and is available as soon as it is first used. The application's data-access role may create, read, browse by key range, update and delete policy records. Define policy file with full maintenance
  • Declare the customer store in deployment configuration. It holds 82-character records keyed by the 10-digit customer number. The application's data-access role may create, read, browse and update customer records but has no delete permission, so a customer delete is refused by the store itself. Define customer file without online deletion
  • This is the same policy-store definition used by another environment's set-up. Keep one shared definition (64-character records, 21-character key, full create/read/browse/update/delete) in configuration that every environment applies, rather than a copy per environment. Define policy file with full maintenance
  • A duplicate of the shared policy-store definition (64-character records, 21-character key, full maintenance) for the second environment set-up. Apply the same single definition. Define policy file with full maintenance
  • This is the same customer-store definition for another environment: 82-character records and a 10-character key, with create, read, browse and update allowed and delete not allowed. Use the shared definition so the no-delete restriction cannot differ between environments. Define customer file without online deletion
  • A duplicate of the shared customer-store definition (82-character records, 10-character key, delete not allowed) for the second environment set-up. Apply the same single definition. Define customer file with deletion prohibited
  • A routing table that maps each entry code to its handler: SSC1 to customer menu (LGTESTC1), SSP1 to LGTESTP1, SSP2 to LGTESTP2, SSP3 to LGTESTP3, SSP4 to LGTESTP4, LGSE to set-up (LGSETUP), LGCF to the customer counter (LGICVS01) and LGPF to the policy counter (LGIPVS01). In the new application these become registered routes or endpoints that run with ordinary user privileges. Define insurance menu and service transactions
  • The same eight-route mapping (SSC1, SSP1 to SSP4, LGSE, LGCF and LGPF to their handlers) for the front-end that users connect to. Keep one route registry shared by the front-end and the services, with no elevated privileges. Map terminal transactions to insurance programs
  • Deployment must replace the configuration, not add to it. Remove the previous application definitions before applying the new routes, so that a redeploy is repeatable and leaves no stale routes or store definitions behind. Map front-end transaction codes to programs
3. Provision the insurance databasedraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 13 criteria

Creates the insurance database: customers and their security details, policies, the endowment, house, motor and commercial product details, and claims. It also sets up automatic numbering of customers, policies and claims starting at 1000001. It is for the administrators who set up an environment. It must create the tables only when the earlier set-up steps ran cleanly, and it must never hand out a duplicate customer, policy or claim number.

As an application administrator, I want the insurance database tables created with automatic numbering when the setup job has run cleanly, so that customers, policies, product details and claims can be stored.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, security. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#3

Open questions

  • SME-009 The claim table has no standard name in the list of data entities. What should the new system call it? (Data architecture)
  • SME-010 Customer, policy and claim numbers are generated automatically. What data type and length must these numbers have? (Data architecture)

Design notes

  • A versioned schema migration creates the customer table (name, date of birth, address, phones, email) and the customer security table (password value, state, password-change count), each with a unique key on customer number. The migration runner stops at the first failed step (severity above 4), so later migrations do not run on a broken schema. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the policy table (customer, issue and expiry dates, policy type, last-changed timestamp, broker id, broker reference, payment, commission). It has a unique key on policy number and a non-unique index on customer number to support lookups of a customer's policies. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the endowment details table, keyed on policy number. A foreign key to the policy table cascades deletes, so deleting a policy removes its endowment details. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the house details table, one row per policy: property type, bedrooms, value, house name, house number and postcode. It has a unique key on policy number and a foreign key to the policy. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the motor details table, one row per policy: make, model, value, registration, colour, engine size, year of manufacture, premium and accidents. It has a unique key on policy number and a foreign key to the policy. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the commercial property table, one row per policy: request, start and renewal dates, address, postcode, location, customer, property type, a peril indicator and premium for each of fire, crime, flood and weather, status and rejection reason. It has a unique key on policy number and a foreign key to the policy. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
  • A migration creates the claim table (claim date, amount paid, claim value, cause, observations) with a unique key on claim number and a foreign key to its policy. It runs only after the earlier migrations succeed. Create the claim table
4. Remove dependent records on deletiondraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 7 rules · 8 criteria

When a customer or a policy is deleted, everything recorded against it is deleted too: policies, their endowment, house, motor and commercial details, their claims, and the customer's security record. It is for insurance operations, who need the records to stay consistent. It must never leave orphaned policies, product details, claims or security records behind.

As an insurance operations manager, I want deleting a customer or policy to remove everything recorded against it, so that no orphaned policy, product, claim or security records remain.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#4

5. Load sample insurance datadraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 13 criteria

Loads a fixed set of sample data for demonstrating and testing the application: ten customers with security records, ten policies, and their endowment, house, motor and commercial cover details. It is for administrators preparing a demo or test environment. The values must be loaded exactly as listed, and the shared sample password value must never reach a production environment.

As an application administrator, I want sample customers, credentials, policies and product details loaded into the database, so that the application can be demonstrated and tested with realistic data.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#5

Open questions

  • SME-011 The sample customers and policies are numbered 1 to 10, but generated customer and policy numbers start at 1000001. Should the sample records keep their numbers below the generated range, or should they get generated numbers? (Data architecture)
  • SME-012 The sample commercial policies have status 1 and the text 'ACTIVE' in the rejection reason field. Is the rejection reason field meant to hold status text? (Business analyst)
  • SME-013 In two sample commercial policies, the renewal date is earlier than the start date (renewal 2011-08-24, start 2011-08-25; renewal 2011-07-30, start 2011-08-01). Is this intended sample data, or is it an error? (Business analyst)
  • SME-014 All ten sample customer logins share the same password value. Should the sample data in the new system keep this shared password? (Security team)
  • DEF-031 Is this intended? The INSERT step has no COND parameter, so it runs even when the table-creation steps were skipped for a return code above 4, and the sample numbers 1 to 10 sit outside the generated range that starts at 1000001. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-033 Confirm this is deliberate: All ten sample customers share one hard-coded password value in the setup job. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-039 Is this intended? The sample commercial rows put 'ACTIVE' into the rejection reason column and give renewal dates a day or two before the start dates (2011-08-24 vs 2011-08-25; 2011-07-30 vs 2011-08-01); the INSERT step also has no COND, so it runs even if the table-creation steps failed. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A seed-data script that runs only in demo and test environments. It inserts customers 1 to 10 with explicit customer numbers, so automatic numbering is not used, and stores a single blank (' ') where a house name, phone or email is absent instead of leaving the field null. Load the ten sample customer profiles
  • Seed script for policies 1 to 10, each with an explicit number and linked to its customer. Types: C for 10, 9 and 7; E for 5 and 4; H for 6 and 8; M for 1, 3 and 2. It uses the listed dates, broker id 0, an empty broker reference, payment 0 and commission 0. Run it after the customer seed so the customer links are satisfied. Register the ten sample policies
  • Seed rows for endowment policies 5 and 4 with the listed values: 5 is N/N/N, 'SHEPPA', term 10, 50000, 'Shep'; 4 is Y/Y/N, 'LIONTMR', term 5, 12500, 'J. MORRIS'. Run after the policy seed. Add endowment details for policies 4 and 5
  • Seed rows for house details on policies 6, 7 and 8 with the listed property type, bedrooms, value, name, number and postcode. Run after the policy seed. Add house property details
  • Seed rows for motor details on policies 1, 3 and 2 with the listed make, model, value, premium, accidents, registration, colour, engine size and year. Run after the policy seed. Add motor vehicle details
  • Seed row for commercial cover on policy 10 ('HURSLEY PARK', 'SO212JN'): fire 3/8000, crime 3/25000, flood 5/2000, weather 4/5000, status 1, and 'ACTIVE' in the rejection reason field, stored exactly as given. Add commercial property cover details
  • Seed row for commercial cover on policy 9 ('TURF MOOR', 'BB104BX'): fire 1/44000, crime 2/25000, flood 3/15000, weather 4/6000, status 1, and 'ACTIVE' in the rejection reason field, stored exactly as given. Add commercial property cover details
6. Prepare monitoring and workload simulationdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria

Prepares the monitoring console's data store and runs a scripted workload against the insurance application. Administrators use it to watch the environment and exercise it under load. Monitoring set-up must be skipped if an earlier set-up step failed badly, and the load run must not turn on its own automatic logging.

As an application administrator, I want the WUI server repository initialised and the GENAPP workload simulation runnable, so that the environment can be monitored and exercised under load.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#6

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-034design noteWhen no earlier step of the repository set-up job ended with a return code above 8, the system shall run EYU9XDUT against the new WUI data repository (EYUDREP) with 'CMASNAME=<CMASAPPL>', 'DAYLIGHT=N', 'TIMEZONE=B', 'SYSID=<CMASYSID>', 'ZONEOFFSET=0' and WUIAPPLID, WUINAME and WUISYSID values, printing a report.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-035design noteIf an earlier step of the repository set-up job ended with a return code above 8, then the system shall skip the WUI repository initialisation step.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-036design noteThe system shall run the workload simulator (ITPENTER) with parameter 'NTWRK=GENAPP', reading initialisation definitions, the concatenated message definitions and the simulation log data set in shared mode, with automatic logging turned off (AUTOLOG dummy) and dumps and printed output sent to the job output.AC-03

Design notes

  • An environment set-up step that initialises the monitoring console's repository with the console and system names and identifiers, daylight saving off, the time zone setting 'B' and a zone offset of 0, and prints a report. In the new application this is provisioning of the monitoring or observability tooling. It runs only when no earlier set-up step failed with a severity above 8. Initialize the WUI server repository
  • An on-demand load-test job that plays the GENAPP scripted scenarios (initialisation definitions plus message scripts) against the application, with the tool's own automatic logging off and its results and diagnostics sent to the job output. In the new application, use a load-testing tool with the scenario scripts kept in version control. Run workload simulation for GENAPP network
7. Validate and register a new policydraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 14 rules · 21 criteria · 2 gaps

Checks an add-policy request, records it as a master policy with a database-assigned policy number, and returns that number and the last-changed timestamp to the caller. It is for policy administrators. It must never create a policy for an unknown request type, for a request too short for its product, or for a customer who does not exist, and each of these failures must return its own code ('99', '98', '70').

As a policy administrator, I want an add-policy request checked, recorded as a master policy and given a policy number, so that only complete requests for known products and existing customers create policies.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#7

Open questions

  • SME-030 When an add-policy request arrives with no request data at all, what should happen: should it be rejected with a specific code, or should processing just stop? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-031 When saving a new policy fails for a reason other than the customer not existing, what outcome code should the caller get back? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-032 What format (data type and length) should the policy number have when the policy data store assigns it? (Data architecture team)
  • SME-034 When adding a policy is rejected for a bad reference, does that always mean the customer does not exist, or can it also mean the broker is unknown? Should an unknown broker be reported differently? (Data architect / DBA)
  • SME-037 After a policy is added, it is passed on to a follow-on step (LGAPVS01). What does that step do for the business, for example keeping a file copy or an audit record? Should the whole add fail if that step fails? (Policy administration SME)
  • SME-038 The name of the person whose life is assured on an endowment policy is supplied as 31 characters but stored in 30. Is it intended that the 31st character is dropped? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-039 New policies are recorded in two places, the policy database and a separate policy file. Does the new system need to keep both, and if so, which one is the official record? (Data architecture team)
  • DEF-005 Is this intended? LGAPOL01, the only caller in the source, always links with a length of 32500, so this check can never fail on that path; it guards only callers that pass the true length. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-006 Is this intended? The length check can never fail when the request comes through LGAPOL01, because LGAPOL01 always links to LGAPDB01 with a fixed length of 32500, so a short request is not caught here. The second 'request not recognised' branch at detail routing is also dead code, since unknown request IDs have already been returned with '99'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-012 Is this intended? After a successful insert, neither the IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL() call nor the read-back of LASTCHANGED is checked for an SQL error, so a failed read-back would still return '00' with a blank or stale timestamp. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Each request has a context object whose result code starts at '00' (success). It carries the request's customer number, which is used both for the policy insert and in any error log entry. Determine policy type and required length
  • Once the database registration finishes without stopping early, pass the full request, including the assigned policy number, to the policy-file writer (LGAPVS01, capability 11) as the next step. A direct service call is enough. The full request is 32,500 bytes in the legacy system, but the new interface needs only the populated request fields. Pass request to follow-on program
8. Store product details for a new policydraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 9 criteria

Stores the endowment, house, motor or commercial details of a new policy under its newly assigned policy number. It is for policy administrators. Details are stored exactly as supplied, with no premium calculated or status derived. If the product details cannot be stored, the whole new policy must be undone so no half-created policy remains.

As a policy administrator, I want the endowment, house, motor or commercial details of a new policy stored under its policy number, so that each policy holds the cover details supplied for its product.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#8

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-047business ruleWhen an Endowment add request ('01AEND') is longer than its required length of 152 bytes (28-byte header plus 124 bytes of endowment details), the system shall store the endowment row for the new policy number with with-profits, equities, managed fund, fund name, term, sum assured and life assured, plus the extra bytes beyond 152 as free-form padding data (PADDINGDATA).AC-01
REQ-F-048business ruleWhen an Endowment add request ('01AEND') is exactly its required length of 152 bytes, the system shall store the endowment row with the same details but without any padding data.AC-02
REQ-F-049error handlingIf the endowment row cannot be stored, then the system shall set return code '90', log the error (date, time, customer and policy number, SQL code, and the first 90 bytes of the request) and end abnormally with code 'LGSQ' so the policy row already added is backed out.AC-03
REQ-F-050business ruleWhen a House add request ('01AHOU') has had its policy row created, the system shall store the house details (property type, bedrooms, value, house name, house number, postcode) under the new policy number.AC-04
REQ-F-051business ruleWhen a motor policy is added, the system shall store the premium and the number of accidents exactly as supplied in the request, without changing the premium for accidents, engine size or vehicle value.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-052business ruleWhen a Commercial add request ('01ACOM') has its policy row created, the system shall store the commercial row for the new policy number with the policy's last-changed timestamp as request date, the issue date as start date and the expiry date as renewal date.AC-07
REQ-F-053design noteThe system shall store the commercial address, postcode, latitude, longitude, customer name, property type, fire, crime, flood and weather perils and premiums, status and rejection reason exactly as supplied, without calculating any premium or deriving any status.AC-08
REQ-F-054error handlingIf the commercial row cannot be stored, then the system shall set return code '90', log the error and end abnormally with code 'LGSQ' so the policy row already added is backed out.AC-09

Open questions

  • SME-033 If the main policy record is saved but saving its type-specific details (endowment, house, motor or commercial) then fails, should the main policy record be removed so that the two are always saved together or not at all? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-035 Motor and house policies are stored with whatever premium the caller supplies. Is the premium meant to be calculated somewhere else before this step, or is it intended that the caller supplies it? (Underwriting / pricing lead)
  • SME-036 When a commercial policy is added, what do its status codes mean (for example, 0 = accepted and anything else = rejected)? Are the premiums for each peril calculated earlier, by the caller or another program, rather than at this step? (Commercial underwriting SME)
  • DEF-003 Is this intended? The only caller in the source (LGAPOL01) always links with a length of 32500, so the request is always treated as carrying 32348 bytes of padding; that is moved into a 3900-byte work field (WS-VARY-CHAR), overrunning it, and the no-padding insert can never be chosen on that path. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-024 Confirm this is deliberate: Return code '90' is set before the abend, but the abend ends the task so the caller never receives it, and the RETURN after each abend can never run. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • A plain field-to-column mapping for the commercial details: address, postcode, latitude, longitude, customer name, property type, the four perils and premiums, status and rejection reason, stored exactly as supplied. There is no rating engine or status derivation in this step. Add commercial policy details

10. Add a policy to the policy databasedraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 8 criteria

The entry point for adding a policy of any product type. It rejects empty or too-short requests, passes valid ones to policy registration, and makes sure that if the product details fail to store, the policy row is undone too. It is for policy administrators. A policy must never be left half-created.

As an insurance policy administrator, I want to add a new policy of any product type with its details, so that the policy is recorded in full and never left half-created.

Open questions

  • SME-030 When an add-policy request arrives with no request data at all, what should happen: should it be rejected with a specific code, or should processing just stop? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-033 If the main policy record is saved but saving its type-specific details (endowment, house, motor or commercial) then fails, should the main policy record be removed so that the two are always saved together or not at all? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • DEF-024 Confirm this is deliberate: Return code '90' is set before the abend, but the abend ends the task so the caller never receives it, and the RETURN after each abend can never run. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Every request that has data starts with result code '00'. Validation and persistence steps overwrite it only when they fail. Default return code to success
  • The entry service checks only that the 28-character header is present, then passes the whole request to the policy registration service (LGAPDB01). That service does the product-specific length check and the inserts inside a single transaction, and the entry service returns its result to the caller. Delegate policy data insert
11. Record a new policy in the policy filedraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 10 criteria · 1 gap

Writes each new policy to the policy file under a key made of its type letter, customer number and policy number, together with a short summary of its product details, so the policy can be found by type, customer and number. It is for policy administrators. It must never overwrite an existing record: a duplicate key or any other write failure returns code '80' and is logged.

As an insurance policy administrator, I want each new policy written to the policy file under its policy key with its type-specific details, so that the policy can be found by type, customer and policy number.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#11

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-062design noteWhen a new policy is added, the system shall key the policy-file record by the policy type letter (the 4th character of the request code: 'E', 'H', 'M' or 'C'), followed by the 10-digit customer number and the 10-digit policy number the database has just assigned.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-063design noteWhen the new policy is an endowment policy (type 'E'), the system shall store the with-profits, equities and managed-fund indicators (one character each), the fund name (10 characters) and the life assured name (30 characters) in the policy-file record.AC-01
REQ-F-064design noteWhen the new policy is a house policy (type 'H'), the system shall store the property type (15 characters), number of bedrooms (3 digits), insured value (8 digits), postcode (8 characters) and only the first 9 characters of the house name in the policy-file record.AC-07
REQ-F-065design noteWhen the new policy is a motor policy (type 'M'), the system shall store the vehicle make (15 characters), model (15 characters), insured value (6 digits) and registration number (7 characters) in the policy-file record.AC-02
REQ-F-066design noteWhen the new policy is a commercial policy (type 'C'), the system shall store the premises postcode (8 characters), the status code (4 digits) and the first 31 characters of the customer name in the policy-file record.AC-08
REQ-F-067design noteWhen the policy details have been assembled, the system shall write a 64-byte record to the policy file (KSDSPOLY) under the 21-character policy key.AC-09
REQ-F-068error handlingIf the policy-file write does not succeed for any reason, including a record with the same key already existing, then the system shall set return code '80' and return to its caller at once.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-069side effectIf the policy-file write fails, then the system shall log a message (through LGSTSQ) with the date, time, program 'LGAPVS01', policy number, customer number, ' Write file KSDSPOLY' and the RESP and RESP2 codes, followed by a second message holding the first 90 bytes of the request ('COMMAREA=').AC-10

Open questions

  • SME-038 The name of the person whose life is assured on an endowment policy is supplied as 31 characters but stored in 30. Is it intended that the 31st character is dropped? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-039 New policies are recorded in two places, the policy database and a separate policy file. Does the new system need to keep both, and if so, which one is the official record? (Data architecture team)
  • DEF-015 Is this intended? If the policy-file write fails, the policy and policy-type rows that LGAPDB01 has already inserted into DB2 are not rolled back, because the program ends with a normal return and no rollback. The policy then exists in DB2 but not in KSDSPOLY, while the caller gets '80'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-025 Confirm this is deliberate: The house name is cut from 20 characters to 9, and the house number is not stored at all in the policy-file record. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-035 Confirm this is deliberate: The commercial customer name is cut from 255 characters to 31, and the address, risk perils and premiums are not stored in the policy-file record. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Build a composite key: the policy type letter, the customer number zero-padded to 10 digits, and the policy number zero-padded to 10 digits, 21 characters in all. Records are then found by keyed lookup on the full key, or by prefix (type, or type plus customer) for range browsing. Build policy record key
  • Map the endowment summary into fixed-width fields: with-profits, equities and managed-fund indicators of 1 character each, fund name of 10 characters and life assured of 30 characters. Values are padded or truncated to those widths. Populate endowment policy details
  • Map the house summary into fixed-width fields: property type of 15 characters, bedrooms of 3 digits, value of 8 digits, postcode of 8 characters, and only the first 9 characters of the house name (truncated on purpose). Populate house policy details
  • Map the motor summary into fixed-width fields: make of 15 characters, model of 15 characters, value of 6 digits and registration of 7 characters. Populate motor policy details
  • Map the commercial summary into fixed-width fields: postcode of 8 characters, status of 4 digits, and the first 31 characters of the customer name. Populate commercial policy details
  • Insert the 64-character summary record into the policy key-value or index store under the 21-character key, using insert-only semantics, so an existing key is never overwritten and the write fails instead. Add policy record to policy store

13. Count transactions by request type and outcomedraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 7 criteria

Counts every insurance transaction by request type and outcome so operations administrators can see how many requests of each kind succeeded or failed. Each event adds one to a single named counter: outcome '00' for return code '00' and '99' for anything else. It must never count an event twice or under the wrong name, and it must count related request types such as '02ACUS' under their shared type.

As an operations administrator, I want every transaction counted by request type and outcome, so that I can see how many requests of each kind succeeded or failed.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#13

Design notes

  • The counter needs a transaction-completed event that carries the request type and the return code as separate fields. Publish it from every request handler when the handler finishes, and have the statistics consumer read these fields first. Statistics event source selection and no-input exit
  • Fallback input: if the event fields are missing, the consumer takes the request type and return code from the request payload that came with the event. Handle both shapes through one input contract instead of two code paths. Statistics event source selection and no-input exit
14. Delete a policydraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 13 rules · 14 criteria

Lets a policy administrator delete a customer's endowment, house, commercial or motor policy. The policy, its type-specific details and its policy-file record are all removed, and a numeric code tells the caller what happened. It must only delete the policy where both the customer number and the policy number match, and it must reject any request type other than the four delete types.

As an insurance policy administrator, I want to delete an endowment, house, commercial or motor policy for a customer, so that the policy and its details are removed from the database and the policy file.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#14

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-078error handlingIf a delete request arrives with no request data at all, then the system shall log 'NO COMMAREA RECEIVED' and abend the transaction with code 'LGCA'.AC-01
REQ-F-079design noteWhen a policy delete request with data is received, the system shall start with return code '00' (success), which stays unless a later check or the database delete sets another code.AC-02
REQ-F-080business ruleIf a policy delete request is shorter than the 28-byte request header, then the system shall set return code '98' and return to the caller without deleting anything.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-081design noteThe system shall convert the request identifier to upper case before checking it, so that lower-case identifiers are accepted the same as upper-case ones.AC-06
REQ-F-082business ruleWhen the upper-cased request identifier is '01DEND', '01DMOT', '01DHOU' or '01DCOM', the system shall pass the whole 32,500-byte request to the policy database module (LGDPDB01) to delete the policy and return that module's return code to the caller.AC-07
REQ-F-083business ruleIf the request identifier is not '01DEND', '01DMOT', '01DHOU' or '01DCOM', then the system shall set return code '99' and delete nothing.AC-14
REQ-F-084business ruleWhen the request type is '01DEND', '01DHOU', '01DCOM' or '01DMOT', the system shall take the customer number and policy number from the request as the delete keys and delete the policy row whose customer number and policy number both match the request.AC-08, AC-09
REQ-F-085design noteWhen a policy row is deleted, the system shall also remove that policy's type-specific details (endowment, house, motor or commercial), because those tables are defined to delete in cascade with the policy.AC-10
REQ-F-086side effectWhen the policy row delete succeeds, the system shall pass the whole request (length 32500) to the policy-file deletion program (LGDPVS01) so that the matching policy-file record is removed too.AC-11
REQ-F-087error handlingIf the database reports anything other than complete success for the policy delete, including no matching policy, then the system shall set return code '90', log an error with date, time, customer number, policy number, SQL code and up to 90 bytes of the request, and return without removing the policy-file record.AC-12, AC-13

Open questions

  • SME-045 Should deleting a policy that no longer exists count as a success or be reported as an error (code 90)? When a policy is deleted, are its type-specific details always deleted with it? (Data architect / DBA)
  • SME-046 A delete-policy request that is shorter than the required 28-character header is described both as returning success ('00') and as being rejected with '98'. Which code should the caller receive? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-047 If removing a policy from the policy file fails during a delete, what outcome should the caller receive? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-048 A delete removes the policy from both the policy database and the policy file. If the first removal succeeds and the second fails, should the first be undone? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-049 When a delete-policy request arrives with no request data at all, what outcome should the caller receive? (Policy administration business analyst)
  • SME-050 Policy deletion rejects short requests with code 98, accepts request types in upper or lower case, and deletes only endowment, motor, house and commercial policies, rejecting anything else with code 99. Is this rule critical to the system's core purpose, or costly if it is wrong? (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-013 Is this intended? The comment says SQL code 100 (policy not found) should count as success because the end result is that the record no longer exists, but the code treats only SQL code 0 as success, so deleting a policy that is already gone returns '90', logs an error and skips the policy-file delete. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Set the response code to '00' as soon as a request with data is accepted. Only a later validation failure or the outcome of the database delete may replace it. Default request outcome to success
  • Compare the request identifier case-insensitively, for example by upper-casing it before matching against '01DEND', '01DMOT', '01DHOU' and '01DCOM', so that '01dend' behaves like '01DEND'. Normalize request identifier to upper case
  • Define the endowment, house, motor and commercial detail tables with a foreign key to the policy table and ON DELETE CASCADE. Deleting the policy row then removes its details in the same transaction, with no separate delete statements. Deleting a policy removes it and its type-specific details together
15. Remove a deleted policy from the policy filedraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 8 criteria

Removes a deleted policy's record from the policy file. The record is found by its key: the policy type letter, the customer number and the policy number. This keeps the policy file in step with the policy database. It must remove only the record with that exact key, and it must report and log a failure, including a record that is not there, instead of passing it silently.

As an insurance policy administrator, I want the policy-file record of a deleted policy removed by its policy key, so that the policy file stays in step with the policy database.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#15

REQ-F-089error handlingIf the policy file delete returns any response other than normal, including record not found, then the system shall set the return code to '81', log the error and return to the caller.AC-04, AC-05

16. Pick a customer number within the control rangedraft · scheduled job · 13 requirements · 12 rules · 12 criteria

Picks an existing customer number at random from within the low and high customer range held in the application control record. Testers and calling programs use it to work with a real customer without knowing one in advance. It must read the range correctly, repair missing control entries with the documented defaults, and never pick a number outside the range unless no customer exists at or above the candidate.

As a tester or calling program, I want a customer number chosen at random within the customer range held in the control queue, so that I can work with an existing customer without knowing one in advance.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#16

REQ-F-092design noteWhen the customer inquiry program was started by another program (the start code begins with 'D' or a calling program name is present), the system shall treat the run as program-called and return its result in the communication area, and otherwise shall receive the terminal input and treat the run as terminal-started.AC-01
REQ-F-093design noteThe system shall start with a customer number range of 1000001 to 1000001, lock the control queue 'GENACNTL' while it reads and repairs it, and release the lock before choosing a customer.AC-02
REQ-F-094design noteWhen the first entry of the control queue 'GENACNTL' can be read, the system shall treat the header entry as present and read every later entry until no more are returned.AC-03

Open questions

  • SME-051 When the control list is first set up, what starting values should be written after 'LOW CUSTOMER=' and 'HIGH CUSTOMER='? (Application business owner)
  • SME-052 When the control list is checked, a read error is treated the same as reaching the end of the list. Should a read error be handled differently, for example so that duplicate low or high customer entries are not written? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-053 The control list is treated as having its header whenever its first entry can be read, even if that entry is not '**** GENAPP CNTL'. Should the new system check the header text? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-054 If writing an entry to the control list fails because storage is unavailable, should the failure be reported, retried or ignored? (Operations team)
  • SME-055 Two runs at the same time could both find a control-list entry missing and both add it. Must runs be made to take turns to prevent duplicates? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-056 The high-customer message shown on the terminal is longer than its 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' label. What should follow the label in that message? (Business analyst for policy lifecycle management)
  • SME-057 When this function is called by another program instead of run from a terminal, what output should it produce, and who should receive it? (Application architecture team)
  • SME-058 This flow is called 'Random Customer Number Retrieval', but no rule says how the customer number is chosen or where it is read from. How should that work? (Business analyst for policy lifecycle management)
  • DEF-016 Is this intended? Only the entries after the first one are checked for 'LOW CUSTOMER' and 'HIGH CUSTOMER', and the first entry is always taken to be the header without checking its text. If the queue exists but the low or high entry is missing, the default 1000001 is written for that end, which can make the low end higher than the high end. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-038 Confirm this is deliberate: The chosen random customer number is shown under the label 'HIGH CUSTOMER=', because the program reuses the high customer field to hold its result. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-051 Is this intended? When the greater-or-equal read finds no customer, the program returns the candidate number, which is not an existing customer, although its header says it returns a customer that is in the file. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Expose one operation that two callers share: a service call that returns the result in its response, and an interactive or terminal entry point that shows the result. Choose the presentation by the entry point, not by checking a start code at run time. Determine invocation mode of the run
  • The customer range starts at 1000001 to 1000001 before the control record is read. Reading and repairing the control record must be serialized with an exclusive lock, such as a row lock or a lock held for the transaction, and the lock must be released before the random customer is chosen. Customer number range is held in a shared control queue and self-initialised
  • Store the control data as a small configuration record with a header, a low customer and a high customer, instead of an ordered queue. If the record is absent, treat all three entries as missing. If it is present, read every entry. Detect existing control queue
  • If the header is missing, write the header marker '**** GENAPP CNTL' as part of the same locked repair of the control record. Write missing header entry
  • If the low customer value is missing, store it as the low end of the range in use, a 10-digit zero-padded number (0001000001 by default), within the same locked repair. Write missing low customer entry
  • If the high customer value is missing, store it as the high end of the range in use, a 10-digit zero-padded number (0001000001 by default), within the same locked repair. Write missing high customer entry
  • For service callers, return a response that holds only the label 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' and the chosen 10-digit customer number, with no data left over from the request. Display high customer message on terminal
17. Look up a customer's policy by typedraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 9 rules · 12 criteria

Finds a customer's policy of a given type in the policy file. It returns either 'Policy Key=' with the full 21-character policy key or a clear 'Policy Bad=' answer. Testers and calling programs use it to get a real policy key. It must never return a policy of a different type from the one asked for.

As a tester or calling program, I want to find a customer's policy of a given type in the policy file, so that I get its full policy key or a clear bad-policy answer.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#17

Open questions

  • SME-066 When a policy lookup fails (bad policy), the reply puts the value 13 in both the customer number and the policy number fields. Is 13 a real value, an error code or a field length, and what do the programs and people that receive this reply expect to find in those fields? (Policy application business analyst)
  • SME-067 When a policy lookup is typed at a terminal, the first 6 characters of the input are dropped to get the policy number. What do those 6 characters represent, and must the new system keep this input format? (Policy application business analyst)
  • SME-068 If the policy lookup input typed at a terminal is empty or shorter than expected (so no policy number is left), what should the system return or show the user? (Policy application business analyst)
  • SME-069 For a policy lookup by policy type and customer number from another program, must callers always send a full 10-digit customer number, or should a shorter number be accepted? And should the lookup pick a policy at random, or is the random value always supplied by the caller (for example the workload driver)? (Workload simulation subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-030 Is this intended? The program blanks a 90-byte caller area without checking the length the caller actually passed, so a shorter caller area would have storage beyond it overwritten. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-036 Is this intended? The program does not check the result of the terminal receive, so a failed or empty receive still goes on to a lookup with blank or partial input. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-037 Confirm this is deliberate: The caller's data length is moved in and immediately overwritten with 11, so the length the caller passed is ignored. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The interactive entry point takes the policy type and the customer number as separate input fields, instead of splitting a typed line at fixed offsets after a 5-character transaction code and space. Accept policy request from terminal
  • The service entry point takes a request with a one-character policy type and a 10-digit customer number as named fields. Accept policy request from calling program
  • Return a fresh response for service callers that holds the result label ('Policy Key=' or 'Policy Bad=') and the 21-character key. Nothing from the caller's request is echoed back. Return result to calling program
18. Reset the application environmentdraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 8 rules · 9 criteria

Lets an operator reset the application to a clean state that matches the restored customer database. The reset sets the customer number range (low 0000000001, high 0000000011 unless the operator gives another high number), seeds the next-customer-number counter, zeroes all 36 transaction statistics counters and clears the operational logs. It must always leave the control record and the next-customer counter in agreement, so that new customers do not collide with restored ones.

As an operator, I want to run the setup transaction to reset the customer number range, statistics counters and operational queues, so that the application matches the restored customer database and starts from a clean state.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#18

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-112business ruleWhen the setup transaction runs, the system shall delete the next-customer-number counter 'GENACUSTNUM' in pool 'GENA' and redefine it with the high customer number (11 unless the operator supplies one), so that the next customer added receives that number.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-113business ruleWhen the operator types more than the 5 characters of the transaction code and separator (for example 'LGSE 250'), the system shall use the characters that follow as the high customer number, writing it to the control queue and seeding the next-customer-number counter with it.AC-06
REQ-F-114business ruleThe system shall always set the low customer number to 0000000001 and, unless the operator supplies a number, the high customer number to 0000000011, matching the restored customer database.AC-07
REQ-F-115side effectWhen the setup transaction runs, the system shall delete and recreate at zero all 36 transaction statistics counters in pool 'GENA', a success '00' and a failure '99' counter for each of 18 request types (such as 'GENA01IMOT00' and 'GENA01IMOT99').AC-03
REQ-F-116design noteWhen the setup transaction runs, the system shall delete the error log queue 'GENAERRS', the start-time queue 'GENASTRT', the statistics queue 'GENASTAT' and the control queue 'GENACNTL', and recreate only 'GENACNTL'; the other queues are rebuilt when the application next writes to them.AC-04
REQ-F-117design noteWhen the operator runs the setup transaction (LGSE), the system shall rewrite the control queue 'GENACNTL' as three entries in order: '**** GENAPP CNTL', 'LOW CUSTOMER=' followed by the 10-digit lowest customer number, and 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' followed by the 10-digit highest customer number.AC-08
REQ-N-003design noteThe system shall write the three control entries with lengths of 20, 23 and 24 characters without waiting if queue space is short, recording each outcome in a response code that is not checked.AC-05
REQ-F-118formattingWhen the setup has finished, the system shall clear the terminal screen, show the high-customer entry (for example 'HIGH CUSTOMER=0000000011') and end the transaction.AC-09

Open questions

  • SME-070 During the setup that resets the customer number range, if writing the control entries fails (for example for lack of space), should the setup stop, report the failure, or carry on? (Application owner)
  • SME-071 During setup, which customer numbers should be recorded as the low and high customer in the control entries, and where should those values come from? (Application owner)
  • SME-072 Should clearing the existing control entries be a stated requirement of the setup, and what should happen if clearing them fails? (Application owner)
  • SME-073 When an operator types a last customer number at setup, should it be checked first (digits only, positive, at most 8 or 10 digits, not below 1) before it resets the customer range and counter, and what should happen if it is invalid? (Operations supervisor)
  • SME-074 Setup resets the customer number range to match a restored database (low 1, high 11 by default, or the operator's value). Is this rule critical to the business, or costly if it were wrong, so that it must be preserved exactly? (Application owner)
  • SME-075 After setup, the first new customer is given number 11, the same as the recorded high customer number. Does the restored database already contain customer 11 (which would cause a duplicate), or is 11 meant to be the first free number? (Customer data owner)
  • DEF-018 Is this intended? Every queue and counter command records a response code that is never tested, so the program shows the 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' completion line even when the control queue write or a counter reset failed. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-057 Is this intended? The override is not checked: non-digit characters or more than 8 digits are moved straight into the 8-digit number, giving an unpredictable or truncated high customer number and counter value. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Reset is an admin operation. It clears the error log, the start-time records and the statistics records, and it rewrites the control record. Only the control record is recreated straight away; the other stores fill again as the application writes to them. Operational log and status queues purged on reset
  • Replace the control record as a whole in one transaction with the header '**** GENAPP CNTL', the 10-digit low customer number and the 10-digit high customer number, so that no reader sees a partly rewritten record. Write control header and customer range entries
  • The legacy writes do not wait for space and never check the result. The new reset should check the write of the control record and report a failure to the operator; the fixed lengths of 20, 23 and 24 characters only matter where the old text format is kept. Write control header and customer range entries
19. Accept and check a policy update requestdraft · scheduled job · 7 requirements · 7 rules · 10 criteria · 1 gap

Checks each policy update request before it reaches the database. The request must be present, of a known type (endowment '01UEND', house '01UHOU' or motor '01UMOT') and long enough for its policy type. Incomplete requests are rejected with code '98'. The checker must never let a short request through to the update, and it must return the database step's code to the caller unchanged.

As a policy administrator, I want each policy update request checked for presence, type and complete data before it is applied, so that incomplete or unrecognised requests are flagged to the caller.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#19

REQ-F-120design noteWhen request data is present, the system shall set the return code to '00' before checking the request.AC-02
REQ-F-121business ruleIf an endowment update request ('01UEND') has less than 152 bytes of request data (28-byte header plus 124-byte endowment details), then the system shall set return code '98' and return to the caller without updating.AC-03, AC-04
