Open questions

  • SME-097 A policy update request is checked for minimum length and routed by request type. Is this rule critical to the business, or costly if it were wrong, so that it must be preserved exactly? (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-029 Is this intended? An unrecognised request type gets return code '99', but the program still links to LGUPDB01, which resets the code to '00'. LGUPDB01 then updates the main policy row (dates, broker) without updating any policy-type table, so the caller may see success and never sees '99'. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Set the response code to '00' as soon as a request with data is accepted, before the length and type checks run. Forward policy update to database program
  • Call the policy database update in-process with the whole validated request, and return its outcome code ('00', '01', '02' or '90') to the caller as the final result. Forward policy update to database program
20. Update a policy in the database with a timestamp checkdraft · scheduled job · 18 requirements · 24 rules · 25 criteria · 2 gaps

Updates a policy's product details (endowment, house or motor) and its common details (issue and expiry dates, broker and broker reference) only if no one else has changed the policy since the caller read it. The check compares the caller's last-changed timestamp with the stored one. It must never overwrite a concurrent change and never alter the payment recorded on the policy, and the caller must get the new last-changed timestamp back.

As a policy administrator, I want a policy's product details and common details updated only when no one else has changed it since I read it, so that concurrent changes are not overwritten.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#20

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-126error handlingIf the policy update database program is called without any request data, then the system shall log the error ' NO COMMAREA RECEIVED' and end the task abnormally with code 'LGCA' (no dump), without attempting any database work.AC-01
REQ-F-127design noteThe system shall start each policy update with outcome '00' and use the request's customer number and policy number to find the policy to update.AC-02
REQ-F-128business ruleWhen the policy row for the customer and policy number is read and its last-changed timestamp equals the one the caller supplied, the system shall update the endowment, house or motor details and then the common policy details, giving the policy a new last-changed timestamp.AC-24
REQ-F-129business ruleWhen the policy row is found and its last-changed timestamp matches the caller's, where the request is a motor update ('01UMOT'), the system shall replace the motor record's make, model, value, registration, colour, CC, year of manufacture, premium and accidents with the request values, matching the record by policy number.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-130business ruleWhen the policy row is found and its last-changed timestamp matches the caller's, where the request is a house update ('01UHOU'), the system shall replace the house record's property type, bedrooms, value, house name, house number and postcode with the request values, matching the record by policy number.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-131business ruleWhen the policy row is found and its last-changed timestamp matches the caller's, where the request is an endowment update ('01UEND'), the system shall replace the endowment record's with-profits, equities, managed-fund and fund-name values, term, sum assured and life assured with the request values, matching the record by policy number.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-132error handlingIf the endowment, house or motor update finds no record for the policy number, then the system shall set outcome '01'.AC-09, AC-10, AC-11
REQ-F-133error handlingIf the endowment, house or motor update fails for any reason other than a missing record, then the system shall set outcome '90' and write an error message with the date, time, customer number, policy number and SQL code, plus up to 90 bytes of the request, to the error log.AC-09, AC-10, AC-12
REQ-F-134error handlingIf the endowment, house or motor update leaves an outcome other than '00', then the system shall close the policy retrieval and return to the caller without updating the common policy record or the policy file, and because the close resets the outcome, the caller receives '00' when the close succeeds.AC-13, AC-14
REQ-F-135business ruleWhen the policy's last-changed timestamp matches the one in the request and no product-detail update has failed, the system shall set the policy's issue date, expiry date, broker ID and broker's reference to the request values and set its last-changed timestamp to the current database timestamp.AC-15
REQ-F-136design noteWhen the policy record has been updated, the system shall read the new last-changed timestamp back, looking the policy up by policy number only, and return it to the caller in the request.AC-16
REQ-F-137error handlingIf reading back the new timestamp fails, then the system shall roll back the whole unit of work, set outcome '90' and log an error message with date, time, customer number, policy number, SQL code and the first 90 bytes of the request.AC-17
REQ-F-138historical artifactThe system shall not store the request's payment amount during a policy update, so that a policy update never changes the payment (or commission) recorded on the policy.AC-18
REQ-F-139business ruleIf the caller's last-changed timestamp differs from the stored policy timestamp, then the system shall change no policy tables and set outcome '02', which the close that follows resets to '00' when it succeeds.AC-25
REQ-F-140error handlingIf no policy row matches the customer and policy number, then the system shall make no database update and set outcome '01', which the close that follows resets to '00' when it succeeds.AC-19
REQ-F-141error handlingIf reading the policy row fails for a reason other than not found, then the system shall set outcome '90' and write an error message with the SQL code to the error log, and the close that follows resets the outcome to '00' when it succeeds.AC-20
REQ-F-142side effectWhen the database update step finishes without an early return, including when the timestamps differ, the policy is not found or the policy read fails, the system shall pass the first 225 bytes of the request to the policy file update, which rewrites the policy file record with the details supplied, and then return to the caller.AC-21, AC-22
REQ-F-143error handlingIf the policy cursor cannot be opened, a product-detail update fails, the cursor cannot be closed, or the update was rolled back, then the system shall return to the caller without calling the policy file update.AC-23

foundyessucceededGap: No rule says what happens if the update of the common policy details itself (issue date, expiry date, broker ID, broker's reference) fails; only failure of the timestamp read-back is covered (R17).

Open questions

  • SME-092 A policy update with an unrecognised request type gets error code '99' but still goes on to update the common policy data, and the '99' is overwritten. Should such requests be stopped before any update? (Policy business analyst)
  • SME-093 If the type-specific part of a policy update (endowment, house or motor) succeeds but the common policy update then fails, nothing is undone. Should both parts succeed or fail together? (Application architect)
  • SME-094 The payment amount is captured on a policy update but thrown away. Should payment be updatable this way? (Policy administration lead)
  • SME-095 After a policy update, the second copy of the policy record is always updated. Should it be updated only when the main database update succeeded? (Mainframe application SME)
  • SME-096 A policy update is rejected if the policy was changed by someone else since it was read (last-changed timestamp check), to stop one user's edit silently overwriting another's. Please confirm this rule is described correctly and must be kept. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-004 Is this intended? The cursor-close routine always overwrites the outcome code with '00', so a timestamp mismatch ('02'), a missing policy ('01') and a read failure ('90') all reach the caller as success, and the motor screen shows 'Motor Policy Updated'. The program also links to LGUPVS01 in these cases, so the policy file is rewritten while the database is not. Separately, after the common policy update the program checks the SQL code of the follow-up timestamp read rather than of the update itself. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-014 Is this intended? The program checks the SQLCODE only after the timestamp read-back SELECT, so a failed UPDATE POLICY is not detected when the read-back succeeds. After the rollback, the cursor (declared WITH HOLD) is closed by the rollback. The CLOSE-PCURSOR step then gets -501, sets the outcome back to '00' and returns, so the caller sees success instead of '90'. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-021 Is this intended? When the timestamps do not match ('02') or the policy is not found ('01'), the program still reaches the LGUPVS01 link, and closing the cursor resets the outcome to '00'. The caller is told the update succeeded although DB2 was not updated. On a timestamp mismatch, the VSAM policy record is rewritten with the request data, so it no longer matches DB2. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-022 Is this intended? When a product-detail update fails with '01' or '90', CLOSE-PCURSOR overwrites the outcome with '00' before the early return. The caller is therefore told the update succeeded although nothing was changed. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-028 Is this intended? When the type-specific update fails with '01' or '90', the cursor-close routine overwrites the code with '00' before the program returns, so the caller is told that the update succeeded. For example, the motor screen shows 'Motor Policy Updated' when nothing was changed. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Start every update with outcome '00'. Find the policy by a keyed lookup on customer number plus policy number, and read it inside the same transaction as the update. Orchestrate policy update and forward request
  • After the update, read the new last-changed timestamp, keyed by policy number, or take it from the update's RETURNING clause, and put it in the response so that the caller can make its next change. Update common policy data and timestamp
21. Synchronise the policy file after an updatedraft · scheduled job · 11 requirements · 12 rules · 12 criteria · 2 gaps

Rewrites a policy's policy-file record with the updated details after a policy update, so that the policy file stays in step with the policy database. It copies the fields for the policy's type (endowment, house, motor or commercial) and blanks the details for any other type. It must replace the whole record, and a failed read or rewrite must stop the update and be logged.

As a policy administrator, I want the policy file record rewritten with the updated policy details, so that the policy file stays in step with the policy database.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, money, personal_data, updates_records. rec/ApplicationDeploymentLifecycleManagement/ApplicationDeploymentandPolicyLifecycleManagement#21

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-144design noteWhen a policy update request is received, the system shall build the policy-file key from the policy type letter (the fourth character of the request ID), the customer number and the policy number, and use the length of the caller's data as the read length.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-145design noteWhen a policy update reaches the policy file step, the system shall read the policy-file record for update using the policy type letter, customer number and policy number from the request as the key.AC-03
REQ-F-146business ruleWhen the policy type is endowment ('E'), the system shall copy the with-profits, equities and managed-fund indicators, the fund name and the life assured from the request into the policy-file record.AC-04
REQ-F-147business ruleWhen the policy type is house ('H'), the system shall copy the property type, number of bedrooms, value, postcode and house name from the request into the policy-file record.AC-05
REQ-F-148business ruleWhen the policy type is motor ('M'), the system shall copy the vehicle make, model, value and registration number from the request into the policy-file record.AC-06
REQ-F-149business ruleWhen the policy type is commercial ('C'), the system shall copy the business postcode, business status and business customer from the request into the policy-file record.AC-10
REQ-F-150business ruleIf the policy type letter is not 'C', 'E', 'H' or 'M', then the system shall blank out the policy details and rewrite the record with blank details.AC-11
REQ-F-151business ruleWhen the record has been read for update, the system shall rewrite the whole policy-file record with the key and the policy details built from the request, replacing all previously stored details.AC-07
REQ-F-152error handlingIf the read for update fails for any reason (record not found or any other file error), then the system shall set return code '81', write an error log entry and abend the transaction with code 'LGV3'.AC-08
REQ-F-153error handlingIf the rewrite of the policy-file record fails, then the system shall set return code '82', write an error log entry and abend the transaction with code 'LGV4'.AC-09

'E', 'H' or 'M'Gap: Fewer fields reach the policy file than the database update changes (for example term and sum assured for endowment, house number for house, colour, CC, year, premium and accidents for motor); confirm whether the policy file should hold only this subset.
any other letterGap: An unrecognised request type passed on by the update service (return code '99') would reach this step and blank the stored policy details; confirm whether that is intended.

Open questions

  • SME-098 If reading or rewriting the second copy of a policy record fails, the program stops abruptly. What result should the caller receive, and should the codes '81' (read failed) and '82' (rewrite failed) be returned? (Policy business analyst)
  • SME-099 The second copy of the policy record receives only some of the policy details on update (for example house number, motor colour, engine size, year, premium, accidents, endowment term and sum assured are left out). Is that intended? (Policy business analyst)
  • DEF-023 Is this intended? The error log has a policy number slot (' PNUM=') that is never filled, so logged failures always show a blank policy number. Also, LGUPDB01 resets the return code to '00' when it closes its cursor and always links to this program, so the policy file can be rewritten even when the database update was refused (policy not found '01' or timestamp mismatch '02'). (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-032 Is this intended? An update request with an unrecognised request ID is not stopped: LGUPOL01 sets return code '99' but still performs the update, and LGUPDB01 overwrites the code with '00', so commercial or unknown types still reach the policy-file rewrite. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-040 Is this intended? An unknown policy type wipes the stored policy details instead of being rejected, because LGUPOL01 does not stop on return code '99' and LGUPDB01 resets it to '00'. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Build the policy-file key from the policy type letter (the fourth character of the request ID), the customer number and the policy number. Use typed fields for the request instead of a length the caller passes in. Derive policy type and customer key
  • Same key as the delete and lookup paths: the type letter, then the 10-digit customer number, then the 10-digit policy number. Put the key build in one shared function so that all policy-file operations agree. Build policy key from request
  • Do a keyed read with a row lock (select for update) on the policy-file record, then a full replace of that record in the same transaction. Rewrite updated policy record

Customer Record Management

Customer Record Creation and Maintenance

1. Accept and check an add-customer requestdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 8 rules · 12 criteria

Receives an add-customer request from customer service and checks it before any customer is created. A request with no data at all is a hard failure that is logged and stops processing, and a request too short to hold the header and the full customer record is rejected with return code '98'. It must never obtain a customer number or create a customer from an empty or incomplete request.

As a customer service user, I want an add-customer request to be checked before a customer is created, so that only complete requests create new customers.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/CustomerRecordManagement/CustomerRecordCreationandMaintenance#1

Open questions

  • SME-015 Every new customer gets the same fixed initial password. Is this shared default password meant to be used in production, and should the new system keep it or create a separate password for each customer? (Security team)
  • SME-024 When an add-customer request is shorter than the required 90 characters, the rules disagree: some say the return code is '98', and others say the request comes back with the default '00'. Which return code must the new system give for a short request? (Business analyst)
  • SME-025 After a new customer is inserted, the customer record is written to the VSAM customer file and a customer security record is created. In what order must these happen, and must both happen for every new customer? (Solution architect)
  • SME-026 Is the VSAM customer file still the main record for any process? If writing to the VSAM file or creating the security record fails after the customer has been inserted into the database, must the database insert be rolled back, and which store is the master copy after a partial failure? (Solution architect)
  • SME-027 When the counter is unavailable, the database generates the customer number instead. What format must customer numbers have, and how is it guaranteed that numbers from the two methods never clash, given that the VSAM customer key is 10 characters? (Data architect)
  • SME-028 Customer security requests with a request type other than '02ACUS' are passed to handling outside this process. Should the new system reject these requests, ignore them, or handle them somewhere else? (Business analyst)

Design notes

  • Start every add-customer response with outcome '00' (success) and a policy count of '00'. Later checks overwrite the outcome only when they fail, so a caller always gets a defined outcome and policy count. Default return code and policy count
  • The customer-add data step must also default its outcome to '00' before it validates the request, so only a failed check or a failed store sets a non-success code. Validate request length and default success
  • Once the request passes the presence and minimum-length checks, the intake hands the complete request to the customer-creation service, which assigns the number and stores the customer. It then returns that service's outcome to the caller unchanged. In the new application this is an internal service call with a typed customer payload, not a fixed 32,500-byte buffer. Delegate customer insertion to database module
2. Assign a customer number and store the new customerdraft · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 7 rules · 7 criteria

Gives each new customer a unique customer number, stores the customer's personal and contact details under it and returns the number to the caller. The number normally comes from a shared counter, and the database assigns it when the counter does not respond. If the customer cannot be stored, the service must return code '90' with no customer number and must not create the customer-file copy or the security record.

As a customer service user, I want each new customer to be stored under a new customer number, so that the customer can be identified in later requests.

Open questions

  • SME-015 Every new customer gets the same fixed initial password. Is this shared default password meant to be used in production, and should the new system keep it or create a separate password for each customer? (Security team)
  • SME-024 When an add-customer request is shorter than the required 90 characters, the rules disagree: some say the return code is '98', and others say the request comes back with the default '00'. Which return code must the new system give for a short request? (Business analyst)
  • SME-025 After a new customer is inserted, the customer record is written to the VSAM customer file and a customer security record is created. In what order must these happen, and must both happen for every new customer? (Solution architect)
  • SME-026 Is the VSAM customer file still the main record for any process? If writing to the VSAM file or creating the security record fails after the customer has been inserted into the database, must the database insert be rolled back, and which store is the master copy after a partial failure? (Solution architect)
  • SME-027 When the counter is unavailable, the database generates the customer number instead. What format must customer numbers have, and how is it guaranteed that numbers from the two methods never clash, given that the VSAM customer key is 10 characters? (Data architect)
  • SME-028 Customer security requests with a request type other than '02ACUS' are passed to handling outside this process. Should the new system reject these requests, ignore them, or handle them somewhere else? (Business analyst)
  • DEF-010 Is this intended? The error message has a customer-number slot that is never filled, so a failed-insert log entry always shows a blank customer number (' CNUM=' followed by spaces), even when the counter had supplied one. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the shared customer-number counter supplies the number, insert the customer row under that explicit key, together with the supplied name, date of birth, address, phone numbers and email. The key must be unique, so a clash with an existing customer is rejected rather than overwritten. Insert customer with counter-issued number
  • Both numbering paths, counter-issued or database-generated, must write the same nine fields: first name, last name, date of birth, house name, house number, postcode, mobile phone, home phone and email. A single insert routine, with the key either supplied or generated, keeps the two paths consistent. Insert customer with counter-assigned number
3. Copy the new customer to the customer filedraft · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria

After a new customer is stored, writes a copy of the full customer record to the customer file, keyed by the 10-digit customer number, so every store holds the same details. If that write fails for any reason, including a customer number that already exists, it must return code '80', log the failure with the request data and stop. It must never leave the failure unrecorded.

As a customer service user, I want each newly added customer to be written to the customer file as well, so that the customer details are held in every store.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerRecordManagement/CustomerRecordCreationandMaintenance#3

REQ-F-010design noteWhen a new-customer request has been inserted successfully, the system shall pass the full 225-byte request data, including the assigned customer number, to the customer copy step.AC-04
REQ-F-011design noteWhen a new customer has been added, the system shall write a 225-byte record to the customer file KSDSCUST, keyed by the 10-digit customer number, holding the customer number, first and last name, date of birth, house name, house number, postcode, number of policies, mobile phone, home phone and email address.AC-01
REQ-F-012error handlingIf the write to the customer file KSDSCUST does not complete normally for any reason (for example the customer number already exists), then the system shall set return code '80', log the failure with its response codes, and abend the task with code 'LGV0' without a dump.AC-02

REQ-F-014side effectWhen a customer file write failure is logged, if request data was received, then the system shall also log 'COMMAREA=' followed by the first 90 bytes of the request, or the whole request if it is shorter than 91 bytes.AC-03

Design notes

  • Call the customer-file copy step only after the customer row is stored, and pass it the whole customer record including the newly assigned number. The step can be an in-process call or a message to the service that owns the customer file, but it must not run when the insert failed. Register customer and hand off to copy program
  • The customer file needs a store keyed by the 10-digit customer number, with one record per customer holding the number, first and last name, date of birth, house name, house number, postcode, number of policies, mobile phone, home phone and email. Adding a customer is an insert-only write, so an existing key must make the write fail. Write new customer record
4. Create the new customer's security recorddraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria

Creates the sign-on security record for every new customer: the customer number, the initial password, a password change count of zero and the state 'N'. Only a new-customer security request (type '02ACUS') may add a record, and any other type is refused with '99'. It must never skip a new customer or add a security record for a request that is not a new-customer request.

As a customer service user, I want a security record to be created for each new customer, so that the customer has sign-on credentials from the start.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, personal_data, security, updates_records. rec/CustomerRecordManagement/CustomerRecordCreationandMaintenance#4

REQ-F-016business ruleWhen the security add request type is '02ACUS' (new customer), the system shall convert the customer number and password change count to numbers and insert the customer number, password, state indicator and password change count into the customer secure table (CUSTOMER_SECURE).AC-02, AC-03
REQ-F-017business ruleIf the security add request type is anything other than '02ACUS', then the system shall set return code '99' and return without adding a record.AC-05
REQ-F-018error handlingIf inserting the security record fails, then the system shall set return code '98', log an error labelled ' INSERT SECURITY' with the SQL code, date and time, and return to the caller.AC-04

  • SME-015 Every new customer gets the same fixed initial password. Is this shared default password meant to be used in production, and should the new system keep it or create a separate password for each customer? (Security team)
  • SME-024 When an add-customer request is shorter than the required 90 characters, the rules disagree: some say the return code is '98', and others say the request comes back with the default '00'. Which return code must the new system give for a short request? (Business analyst)
  • SME-025 After a new customer is inserted, the customer record is written to the VSAM customer file and a customer security record is created. In what order must these happen, and must both happen for every new customer? (Solution architect)
  • SME-026 Is the VSAM customer file still the main record for any process? If writing to the VSAM file or creating the security record fails after the customer has been inserted into the database, must the database insert be rolled back, and which store is the master copy after a partial failure? (Solution architect)
  • SME-027 When the counter is unavailable, the database generates the customer number instead. What format must customer numbers have, and how is it guaranteed that numbers from the two methods never clash, given that the VSAM customer key is 10 characters? (Data architect)
  • SME-028 Customer security requests with a request type other than '02ACUS' are passed to handling outside this process. Should the new system reject these requests, ignore them, or handle them somewhere else? (Business analyst)
  • SME-029 What do security state 'N' and the count field mean (for example, 'N' means new or must change password, and count means failed logins)? What other states exist, and which process increases the count and moves a customer out of state 'N'? (Security officer)
  • DEF-041 Is this intended? The caller (LGACDB01) does not check the return code after linking to LGACDB02, so a failed security insert leaves a new customer without a security record and the failure is not reported to the user. (Subject-matter expert)

5. Accept a customer update requestdraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 4 rules · 4 criteria

Receives customer update requests from customer service and accepts only genuine update requests (type '01UCUS'). Each accepted request goes to the update service, and that service's outcome comes back to the caller. Any other request type must be refused with return code '99' and never change customer details.

As a customer service user, I want customer update requests to be checked for their type, so that only genuine update requests change customer details.

6. Update the customer's personal and contact detailsdraft · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 5 criteria

Updates an existing customer's name, date of birth, address, phone numbers and email in the customer database, then passes the change on so that the customer file is updated too. Every supplied field replaces the stored one, so a blank field blanks the stored value. An unknown customer must return '01' with no error log, and any other failure must return '90' and be logged.

As a customer service user, I want to update an existing customer's personal and contact details, so that the stored customer record stays current.

Design notes

  • Default the outcome to '00', then update the customer row found by a keyed lookup on the customer number in the request. The update has to tell 'no matching row' (outcome '01') apart from any other database failure (outcome '90'). Default outcome to success and update
  • When the database update step has finished, hand the customer record (225 bytes of customer data) and its return code to the customer-file update step, which brings the customer file into line with the database. Pass request to follow-on program
7. Replace the customer's record in the customer filedraft · service · 3 requirements · 3 rules · 3 criteria

Keeps the customer file in line with a customer update by replacing the customer's whole stored record with the updated data, found by customer number and locked while it is changed. If the record cannot be read for update, including when the customer is not on the file, the service returns '81'. If the rewrite fails, it returns '82'. Both failures are logged and stop processing, and it must never apply a partial update.

As a customer service user, I want a customer update to also replace the customer's record in the customer file, so that the customer file matches the updated details.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, personal_data, updates_records. rec/CustomerRecordManagement/CustomerRecordCreationandMaintenance#7

Diagnostic and Error Message Logging

1. Accept log requests from programs and terminalsdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 4 rules · 6 criteria

Gives every part of the application, and operators at a terminal, one shared way to record a diagnostic or error message. Each message is stamped with the identifier of the system that produced it, and the submitter gets the acknowledgement that suits how they sent it: a program call returns quietly, a terminal entry clears the screen. It must never lose or garble the submitted text: program messages keep up to 90 characters, terminal messages keep the 74 characters after the 5-character transaction code.

As an application component or terminal operator, I want to submit a diagnostic or error message to the shared logger, either by calling it from a program or by entering it at a terminal, so that the message is recorded and I get the right acknowledgement for how I submitted it.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/No domain/DiagnosticandErrorMessageLogging#1

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-001design noteWhen the logging program is called by another program, the system shall treat it as a program call (mode 'C'), build the log record as the CICS system identifier, one space, then the caller's message text (up to 90 characters), and use the caller's data length plus 5 as the record length.AC-03, AC-04
REQ-F-002design noteWhen the logging program is started from a terminal rather than by another program, the system shall read the terminal input, treat it as a terminal request (mode 'R'), drop the first 5 characters (the transaction code), use the next 74 characters as the message text, and use the received length minus 5, plus 5, as the record length.AC-05, AC-06
REQ-F-003formattingWhen the log request was entered at a terminal (mode 'R'), the system shall, after writing the queues, clear the screen by sending a single blank character, unlock the keyboard and end the task.AC-01
REQ-F-004design noteWhen the logger was called by another program (mode 'C'), the system shall return to the caller without any screen output.AC-02

Open questions

  • SME-076 When a message is written to the error log, the system drops fixed numbers of characters (5 from terminal input, 7 when a 'Q=' queue directive is removed, and adds 5 back before writing). What do these characters represent: the system identifier, the 'Q=' prefix, the 4-character queue code, and is there a separator after the queue code? Must the new system keep this exact input format, or can it define an explicit one? (Application support team)
  • SME-077 If writing a message to the error log queue fails, including when there is not enough storage, what should happen: stop, report it, retry, or ignore it? (Application support team)
  • SME-078 When the error logger is run directly from a terminal, it sends a blank reply to clear the screen and unlock the keyboard. Should this be kept as a requirement, and what should replace it in the new system? (Application owner / business analyst)
  • SME-079 A 'Q=' directive replaces part of the default error queue name 'GENAERRS' with a 4-character code. Which characters of the queue name are replaced? (Application support team)
  • SME-080 Should log messages be limited to a maximum length (for example 90 characters), and should a message from a calling program that is longer than that be rejected or cut short? (Application owner for error logging)
  • DEF-001 Is this intended? The record length is taken from the caller's commarea length while the message area holds only 90 characters: callers that pass their 99-byte 'COMMAREA=' message (LGAPOL01, LGDPVS01 and others) get a length of 104 for a 95-byte record, so the logged record runs past the record into neighbouring storage and the last 9 characters of the caller's text are lost. On terminal entry the input area is 79 bytes but up to 80 are requested. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Expose the logger as a callable service (in-process API or endpoint) that takes a message of up to 90 characters. The service prefixes the identifier of the producing system/instance and one space, and records the length as message length plus 5. Keep the 90-character limit and the 'system-id space text' layout so existing log readers still work. Use caller-supplied text as message
  • Give operators a separate entry point (a console command or simple form) for typing a message by hand. When the input still carries a 5-character command/transaction prefix, strip it and keep at most the next 74 characters as the message. Then pass it through the same record-building path, with length computed as input length minus 5, plus 5. Use terminal input as message
  • A program-call submission must return straight to the caller with no user-facing output and no result the caller has to handle. Make it a fire-and-forget call that does not change the caller's flow. Terminal acknowledgement for directly entered log requests
2. Record log messages to the standard and error queuesdraft · service · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 6 criteria · 1 gap

Writes every diagnostic and error message to the standard system log, and also to an application error queue that support staff review. The error queue is 'GENAERRS' by default, but a caller can redirect a message to another queue by starting it with 'Q=' and a 4-character code. It must never block or fail the calling business transaction: messages go to both destinations, but a write that fails or has no room is dropped silently.

As an operations or support team member, I want every diagnostic and error message written to the standard log queue and to an error queue that callers can redirect, so that I can find and review application errors.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit. rec/No domain/DiagnosticandErrorMessageLogging#2

Transaction Statistics and Monitoring

1. Self-scheduled statistics refreshdraft · scheduled job · 4 requirements · 2 rules · 4 criteria

The statistics collector runs on a one-minute cycle. Each run notes the time of the previous run, records how many seconds have passed since then, and saves the current time for the next run, so operations staff always have fresh throughput figures. It must not miss its next run, and when no previous time has been saved it must use 12:00:00 ('120000') as the previous time.

As an operations monitor, I want the statistics collector to restart itself every minute and record how long it has been since its last run, so that the throughput statistics stay continuously refreshed.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/No domain/TransactionStatisticsandMonitoring#1

REQ-F-002side effectThe system shall retrieve the previous run time from the '000V' statistics queue and replace the stored time with the current time.AC-02
REQ-F-003side effectIf no previous run time is available in the '000V' statistics queue, then the system shall default the previous run time to '120000'.AC-03
REQ-F-004side effectThe system shall store the elapsed seconds, calculated as (current hours×3600 + minutes×60 + seconds) minus the same for the previous run time.AC-04

Open questions

  • SME-100 The web statistics queue names appear to start with 'GENA'. What exact prefix is used for every statistics queue name? (Operations)
  • SME-101 If the system can't read a statistic's previous value (for example on the first run, or when the queue is empty), the legacy system uses whatever comes back without checking it. Should the new system set the previous value to zero instead? (Business analyst)
  • SME-102 The time since the last statistics refresh is worked out from the time of day only. A refresh that spans midnight therefore gives a negative or wrong interval, and the '120000' default gives a meaningless interval on the first run. Should the new system keep this behaviour or correct it? (Business analyst)
  • SME-103 What starts the web statistics refresh, and how often does it run? (Operations)
  • DEF-066 Is this intended? The program does not check whether the restart was scheduled. If the START fails, the one-minute cycle stops without any message. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The new application needs a scheduled job that starts the statistics collection once a minute. The legacy run books its own next run first, before it reads any counters, and never checks whether the booking worked. A scheduler with a fixed one-minute interval, such as a cron trigger or a timer service, replaces that self-booking. It must still run every minute even if a run fails partway, so that one failure does not stop the cycle. Statistics collector re-schedules itself every minute
2. Total transaction counters by outcome and typedraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 6 criteria

Each run totals the GENA transaction counters by outcome and by type: a successful-transaction total, an error total, and inquiry, add, update and delete totals. Business monitor users read these totals to follow throughput. The new application must not get the membership of each total wrong: success totals use only the 17 counters ending '00', the error total uses only the 17 ending '99', 'GENAOTHER' is in neither, update has no customer or commercial counter, and delete has no customer counter.

As a business monitor user, I want the transaction counters in pool 'GENA' totalled into successful, error, inquiry, add, update and delete totals, so that I can see transaction throughput by outcome and type.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/No domain/TransactionStatisticsandMonitoring#2

3. Publish statistics to shared queuesdraft · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 6 rules · 4 criteria

Each run publishes every success counter, every type total and the customer-number counter to its own named shared queue. Each queue holds three items: the new value, the previous value and the change between them, so dashboards can show current performance and movement since the last refresh. The new application must keep the queue names, the order of the three items and the change calculation exactly the same. It must never publish error counters, the error total or 'GENAOTHER'.

As a business monitor user, I want each statistic published to its own shared queue with its new value, previous value and change, so that dashboards can show current performance counters and how they moved since the last refresh.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/No domain/TransactionStatisticsandMonitoring#3

Requirements

Open questions

  • SME-100 The web statistics queue names appear to start with 'GENA'. What exact prefix is used for every statistics queue name? (Operations)
  • SME-101 If the system can't read a statistic's previous value (for example on the first run, or when the queue is empty), the legacy system uses whatever comes back without checking it. Should the new system set the previous value to zero instead? (Business analyst)
  • SME-102 The time since the last statistics refresh is worked out from the time of day only. A refresh that spans midnight therefore gives a negative or wrong interval, and the '120000' default gives a meaningless interval on the first run. Should the new system keep this behaviour or correct it? (Business analyst)
  • SME-103 What starts the web statistics refresh, and how often does it run? (Operations)
  • SME-104 Should the GENACUSTNUM statistic be read as the number of customers? It is really the counter that hands out customer numbers, so it includes its starting value and customers who have since been deleted. (Business analyst)
  • SME-105 Should the 'GENAOTHER' transaction counter count as a success, as an error, or as neither? And should total errors also be published as a statistic? Today the total is calculated but never stored. (Operations)
  • DEF-002 Is this intended? The change value is stored in an unsigned field. When a counter falls below its previous value (for example after the counters are reset), the change is recorded as a positive number with no minus sign. Also, the program does not check whether reading the previous value succeeded. On the first run, when the queue does not exist yet, the 'previous' value is whatever was left in the work field from the last queue handled. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-053 Is this intended? The program counts errors but never publishes the total, so a monitor cannot see error volume. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Each statistic needs a small keyed record, keyed by its queue name (for example 'GENA100V' or 'GENAX00V'), that holds the current value, the previous value and the change. Publishing reads the stored current value as the previous value and then replaces the whole record with new, previous and change (new minus previous). Do this as one atomic replace, such as a keyed upsert in a cache or table, so readers never see an empty or half-written statistic. Keep the order new, previous, change wherever consumers read it as a list. Publish transaction type totals
4. Business-monitor symbol list (not delivered)draft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria

The legacy collector builds a business-monitor symbol list of the counter values and the region's APPLID, then ends without sending it or the 'GENAST3TEMP' template anywhere. That list is the only place the error total, the individual error counters and 'GENAOTHER' ever appear. The team must not assume any business monitor, queue or screen receives these values today, and must not treat the start-time entry as filled in.

As a business monitor user, I want to know that the business-monitor symbol list is built but never delivered, so that I do not rely on it for error totals or the region's APPLID.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/No domain/TransactionStatisticsandMonitoring#4

Design notes

  • A scheduled or on-demand job reads the simulator log in shared, read-only mode, so other runs can read it at the same time. It formats the records with the same options as today: console, SNA formatting, display, data, run and end. If the simulator is retired, this job goes with it. Produce the simulator log listing
  • The formatted listing goes to the job's printed report output (print class A today) and is kept where operators can view it. The job opens the simulator log as input only and needs no write access to it. Produce the simulator log listing

3. Look up customer detailsdraft · scheduled job · 8 requirements · 11 rules · 13 criteria

Looks up one customer by customer number for customer service users and calling applications. It returns the customer's name, date of birth, address, phone numbers and email. It must return '98' for a request shorter than 90 bytes, '01' for an unknown customer, and '90' with an error log entry for any other database failure. A request with no data must be logged as ' NO COMMAREA RECEIVED' and end with code 'LGCA'.

As a customer service user, I want to retrieve a customer's details by customer number, so that I can see who the customer is and how to contact them.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, personal_data. rec/Unassigned-Programs#3

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-006error handlingIf a customer inquiry is started with no request data (a length of zero), then the system shall log the message ' NO COMMAREA RECEIVED' with the date and time to the error queue and end the transaction abnormally with abend code 'LGCA' without a dump.AC-01, AC-02
REQ-F-007business ruleWhen a customer inquiry request with data is received, the system shall first set the return code to '00' (success) and the number of policies to '00' before checking the request length.AC-03, AC-04, AC-05
REQ-F-008business ruleIf a customer inquiry request is shorter than 90 bytes (customer record length 72 plus header and trailer length 18), then the system shall return to the caller with return code '98' without looking up the customer.AC-04, AC-05, AC-06, AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-009design noteWhen a customer inquiry request is at least 90 bytes long, the system shall pass the whole request (32500 bytes) to the customer database service (LGICDB01) to look up the customer and return its result to the caller.AC-09
REQ-F-010business ruleWhen a customer inquiry passes the request checks, the system shall look up the customer by customer number in the CUSTOMER table and return first name, last name, date of birth, house name, house number, postcode, mobile phone, home phone and email address, with return code '00'.AC-10
REQ-F-011business ruleIf no customer exists with the requested customer number (SQLCODE 100), then the system shall return code '01' without writing an error log entry.AC-11
REQ-F-012error handlingIf the customer lookup fails because of a database deadlock or timeout (SQLCODE -913), then the system shall return code '01', the same code as customer not found, without writing an error log entry.AC-12
REQ-F-013error handlingIf the customer lookup fails with any other database error, then the system shall return code '90' and write an error log entry with date, time, customer number and SQLCODE, followed by up to the first 90 bytes of the request, via the logging program (LGSTSQ).AC-13

Open questions

  • DEF-007 Confirm this is deliberate: The only caller in the source (LGICUS01) always links with a length of 32500 and already makes the same 90-byte check itself, so this check can never fail in practice. It is a defensive duplicate. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-008 Is this intended? Error log entries written by LGICDB01 carry the program name ' LGICUS01', not LGICDB01, so database errors look as if they came from the front-end program. Also, a deadlock or timeout (-913) returns the same '01' code as customer not found, so callers report a temporary database problem as a missing customer. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-060 Is this intended? The logged message names the program as ' LGICUS01' rather than LGICDB01. Also, the only caller in the source always passes 32500 bytes, so this abend cannot be triggered through the application. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Every customer inquiry reply starts as a success: return code '00' and number of policies '00' are set before any check runs. Later checks overwrite them only on failure. Default success outcome and policy count
  • Once a request passes the length check, the inquiry calls the customer data service (LGICDB01 today) with the whole request (32500 bytes today). It passes that service's reply and return code back to the caller unchanged. In the new application this is a call from the inquiry API to the customer lookup service, keyed by customer number. Delegate customer lookup to database service
4. Route policy inquiries by request typedraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 11 rules · 12 criteria

Sends each policy inquiry to the right lookup for its request ID. The lookups are endowment, house, motor, and four commercial searches: by customer and policy, by policy number alone, by customer, and by postcode. The request ID must match in any letter case. Any ID other than '01IEND', '01IHOU', '01IMOT', '01ICOM', '02ICOM', '03ICOM' or '05ICOM' must get code '99' and no policy data.

As a customer service user, I want my policy inquiry routed to the right lookup for the policy type I ask for, so that I get the correct endowment, house, motor or commercial policy information.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data. rec/Unassigned-Programs#4

Open questions

  • SME-059 When commercial policies are listed by customer (03ICOM) or by postcode (05ICOM), should the caller get every matching policy or only one? Should the list by customer stop at 20 policies (today a 21st can slip through), and should the postcode search also be limited? (Commercial underwriting SME)
  • DEF-056 Confirm this is deliberate: LGIPDB01's no-request-area abend (LGCA) is defensive code that cannot fire through its only caller, which checks the same condition first and always passes 32500 bytes. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Every policy inquiry reply starts with return code '00'. Only a later failure (not found, reply area too small, database error or unknown request) changes it, so a request that runs cleanly always returns '00'. Missing request area aborts the transaction
  • At the start of each policy inquiry, the supplied customer number and policy number become the lookup keys. They are also kept as context for error messages, so any error logged later names the customer and policy the caller asked for. Prepare inquiry keys and default outcome
5. Report policy lookup outcomesdraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 8 criteria · 2 gaps

Tells customer service users and calling applications why a policy could not be returned: '01' when the customer or policy does not match, '98' when the caller's reply area is too small, and '90' when the database failed. A plain not-found must never be logged. Every '90' failure must reach the error log with the customer, policy, lookup and database code, so support staff can investigate.

As a customer service user, I want a clear outcome code when a policy cannot be returned, so that I know whether the policy does not exist, my request area was too small, or the system failed, and support staff can investigate failures.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches audit, personal_data. rec/Unassigned-Programs#5

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-024error handlingIf no policy matches the customer number and policy number for the requested policy type, then the system shall set return code '01' (customer or policy not valid) and write no error log.AC-01
REQ-F-025error handlingIf a commercial inquiry by policy number alone ('02ICOM') finds no matching policy, then the system shall return code '01'.AC-02
REQ-F-026error handlingIf the policy lookup fails for any reason other than no matching policy, then the system shall set return code '90' and write an error log.AC-03
REQ-F-027error handlingIf a commercial inquiry by policy number alone ('02ICOM') fails for any reason other than the policy not existing, then the system shall return code '90' and write an error message with date, time, customer number, policy number and database code to the error log queue.AC-04
REQ-F-028side effectWhen a policy lookup fails with return code '90', the system shall send the error log program (LGSTSQ) a message with date, time, 'LGIPDB01', customer number, policy number, the lookup label (' SELECT ENDOW ', ' SELECT HOUSE ', ' SELECT MOTOR ' or ' SELECT Commercial ') and the database code, then a second message with up to the first 90 bytes of the request.AC-07, AC-08
REQ-F-029error handlingIf the caller's request area is smaller than the space needed for the endowment reply, then the system shall set return code '98' and return to the caller without any policy details.AC-05, AC-06

6. Return policy detailsdraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 10 rules · 15 criteria

Returns the full details of an endowment, house, motor or commercial policy, so customer service users can answer questions about cover, dates and premiums. A policy must be returned only when its policy number belongs to the given customer number and it has details of the requested type. An empty broker ID or payment must come back as zero, and commercial dates must be reported as issue (start date), expiry (renewal date) and last-changed (request date).

As a customer service user, I want the details of a customer's endowment, house, motor or commercial policy returned to me, so that I can answer questions about the policy's cover, dates and premiums.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data. rec/Unassigned-Programs#6

Open questions

  • SME-059 When commercial policies are listed by customer (03ICOM) or by postcode (05ICOM), should the caller get every matching policy or only one? Should the list by customer stop at 20 policies (today a 21st can slip through), and should the postcode search also be limited? (Commercial underwriting SME)
  • SME-060 When a policy has no broker or payment recorded, should the inquiry return zero, or show it as 'not set'? Should a missing broker reference be handled the same way? (Policy administration lead)
  • SME-061 A commercial policy inquiry reports the policy's request date as its 'last changed' time, which is used elsewhere to stop two people overwriting each other's changes. Is that intended, or should 'last changed' come from the main policy record? (Data architect / DBA)
  • DEF-017 Confirm this is deliberate: The '98' reply-too-small check can never trigger: the only caller, LGIPOL01, always passes a 32500-byte area, far more than the 1207 bytes needed. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Before replying, the inquiry works out the space the reply needs: 33 bytes of header plus the length for the policy type. That is 124 for endowment plus any padding data, 130 for house, 137 for motor and 1174 for commercial. In a message-based API this becomes a check that the reply fits the caller's limit, with '98' when it does not. Retrieve house policy and size reply
  • For an endowment policy, the space needed is 33 + 124 bytes plus the length of the policy's free-form padding data when present. The padding length must be read with the policy, so the size check and the reply use the same value. Retrieve endowment policy and size response
  • An endowment reply ends with the end-of-data marker 'FINAL', written straight after the padding data: at position 1 plus the padding length, or position 1 when there is none. Callers use it to find where the policy data ends. An API with explicit field lengths may not need it, but it must stay while existing callers read it. Mark end of endowment policy data
7. Look up a single commercial policydraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 8 criteria · 4 gaps

Returns one commercial policy to policy administrators, found by customer and policy number or by policy number alone. It shows the policy's peril values, premiums, status and owning customer exactly as stored, with no recalculation. When the policy is found by policy number alone, the reply must name the customer who owns it, not the one the caller supplied, and a reply area smaller than 33 + 1174 bytes must get code '98'.

As a policy administrator, I want to retrieve a commercial policy by customer and policy number or by policy number alone, so that I can see its stored peril values, premiums, status and owning customer.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/Unassigned-Programs#7

Open questions

  • SME-059 When commercial policies are listed by customer (03ICOM) or by postcode (05ICOM), should the caller get every matching policy or only one? Should the list by customer stop at 20 policies (today a 21st can slip through), and should the postcode search also be limited? (Commercial underwriting SME)
  • SME-062 What are the valid status values for a commercial policy and what does each mean (for example quoted, accepted, rejected)? Which part of the system sets them? (Commercial underwriting SME)
  • SME-063 Anyone with a policy number can look up a commercial policy (02ICOM) without any check that the policy belongs to their customer. Is this meant to be a back-office lookup? Should the new system check customer ownership or user role? (Security / compliance officer)
  • DEF-017 Confirm this is deliberate: The '98' reply-too-small check can never trigger: the only caller, LGIPOL01, always passes a 32500-byte area, far more than the 1207 bytes needed. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-026 Confirm this is deliberate: An inquiry by policy number alone returns any commercial policy, and the owning customer's number, to the caller, without checking that the caller's customer owns the policy. The header comment and the calling screen (which uses '02ICOM' only when no customer number is given) show this is intended as a lookup by policy number. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • In a '01ICOM' or '02ICOM' reply, the marker 'FINAL' goes in the first 5 positions of the free space after the rejection reason, so callers can find where the data ends. Keep it in the reply layout while existing callers depend on it. Return commercial policy by customer and policy
8. List commercial policies by customer or postcodedraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 7 criteria · 1 gap

Searches commercial policies for policy administrators by customer number ('03ICOM') or by property postcode ('05ICOM'). As built today, the reply holds only the last policy read: a customer search stops after the 21st policy, a postcode search reads every match, and no match still returns code '00'. A search that cannot be started must return '89', and one that cannot be closed must return '88', each with an error message logged.

As a policy administrator, I want to search commercial policies by customer or by property postcode, so that I can find commercial policies matching those criteria.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches money, personal_data, reporting_only. rec/Unassigned-Programs#8

REQ-F-046business ruleWhen more than 20 commercial policies have been read for a customer inquiry ('03ICOM'), the system shall stop reading after the 21st row, leaving the 21st row in the response and the return code at '00'.AC-02, AC-03

11. Customise installation members with site valuesdraft · service · 36 requirements · 36 rules · 38 criteria

Fills in the placeholders in the GenApp installation templates with the values the installer configured for their site, so the templates work in that environment. The placeholders stand for library names, region and system identifiers, database names and file paths. Every placeholder must get the value of its own setting and none may be left behind. '<WSIMLOG>', '<WSIMSTL>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSDBRM>' and '<PDSMSGS>' must take the simulator product qualifier, as they do today, not the library name they suggest.

As an installer, I want placeholders in the GenApp installation members replaced with my site's configured values, so that the members can be used in my environment.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk high; touches security. rec/Unassigned-Programs#11

Open questions

  • DEF-042 Is this intended? MAC1 fetches the log data set name (WSIMLOG) from the pool, but it replaces '<WSIMLOG>' with WSIMHLQ instead. Lines 41-46 do the same for '<PDSDBRM>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSLOAD>', '<PDSMSGS>' and '<WSIMSTL>'. This looks like a copy-and-paste slip. It does no harm today because no member uses these placeholders. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-045 Is this intended? Lines 41-46 replace the library placeholders '<PDSDBRM>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSLOAD>', '<PDSMSGS>', '<WSIMLOG>' and '<WSIMSTL>' with the simulator qualifier (WSIMHLQ) rather than with their own library names, which are fetched at line 13 but never used. CUST1 also misspells PDSMAPC as PDSMACP when it pools the value. No template uses these placeholders today, so nothing goes wrong now, but any template that used them would get the wrong library. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-046 Is this intended? '<PDSDBRM>' is replaced with the simulator qualifier (WSIMHLQ) instead of the DBRM library name that CUST1 pools under PDSDBRM. This is part of the same copy-paste pattern as lines 41-46. No template uses the placeholder today. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-047 Is this intended? The placeholders '<PDSDBRM>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSLOAD>', '<PDSMSGS>', '<WSIMLOG>' and '<WSIMSTL>' are all replaced with the WSim product qualifier (WSIMHLQ), even though their own values are retrieved on line 13 and set in CUST1. This looks like a copy-and-paste slip, so any member that uses these placeholders gets the wrong data set name. (Subject-matter expert)
  • DEF-048 Is this intended? MAC1 replaces the placeholders '<PDSDBRM>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSLOAD>', '<PDSMSGS>', '<WSIMLOG>' and '<WSIMSTL>' with the Workload Simulator qualifier WSIMHLQ. It ignores the GenApp library names that CUST1 builds and passes for these same variables, and that MAC1 itself reads in. No shipped member uses these placeholders, so nothing goes wrong today, but any member that did would get the wrong data set name. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Template substitution: every '<LOADX>' is replaced with the GenApp load library name, which is the installation qualifier followed by '.LOAD'. Derive the value from the one qualifier setting rather than asking for it separately. Replace load library placeholder in member
  • Template substitution: every '<AORSYSID>' is replaced with the application-owning region system identifier from the site configuration. Substitute application-region system identifier placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<DB2RUN>' is replaced with the configured database run library value from the site configuration. Replace run placeholder with configured value
  • Template substitution: every '<TORAPPL>' is replaced with the terminal-owning region application identifier from the site configuration. Replace tor application placeholder in member
  • Template substitution: every '<SOURCEX>' is replaced with the GenApp source library name, which is the installation qualifier followed by '.SRC'. Derive the value from the qualifier setting. Replace source placeholder with environment name
  • Template substitution: every '<TORSYSID>' is replaced with the terminal-owning region system identifier from the site configuration. Substitute tor system identifier placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<ZFSHOME>' is replaced with the configured file-system home directory. Replace home directory placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<DB2DBID>' is replaced with the configured database name. Replace database id placeholders in member
  • Template substitution: every '<WSIMMSX>' is replaced with the GenApp message-text library name, which is the installation qualifier followed by '.MSGTXT'. Derive the value from the qualifier setting. Replace placeholder with session value
  • Template substitution: every '<DORAPPL>' is replaced with the data-owning region application identifier from the site configuration. Substitute data-owning region application name
  • Template substitution: every '<CICSHLQ>' is replaced with the configured transaction-server library prefix. Substitute transaction-server prefix placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<KSDSCUS>' is replaced with the customer data file name the installer set up. Replace customer dataset placeholder throughout member
  • Template substitution: every '<COBOLHLQ>' is replaced with the site's COBOL compiler library qualifier. Substitute COBOL library qualifier placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<WSIMHLQ>' is replaced with the site's workload simulator library qualifier (shipped as 'PP.WSIM.V110'). Several other placeholders reuse this same value. Replace WSIM qualifier placeholder throughout member
  • Template substitution: every '<USRHLQ>' is replaced with the installing user's data set qualifier. Replace user qualifier placeholders in member
  • Template substitution: every '<WSIMWSX>' is replaced with the name of the GenApp workload simulator script library. A template without the placeholder passes through unchanged. Replace placeholder throughout edited member
  • Template substitution: every '<SQLID>' is replaced with the database SQL authorisation ID set for the installation. Replace authorization identifier placeholders
  • Template substitution: every '<CPSMHLQ>' is replaced with the site's CICSPlex SM library qualifier. Substitute management-component prefix placeholder
  • Template substitution: every '<DB2CCSID>' is replaced with the database coded character set ID set for the installation. Substitute character-set placeholder everywhere
  • Template substitution: every '<DB2PLAN>' is replaced with the database plan name set for the installation. Replace plan placeholder throughout member
  • Template substitution: every '<WSIMSTL>' is replaced with the WSim product high-level qualifier (WSIMHLQ), not with the GenApp WSim data set name. Keep that mapping unless the owner decides otherwise. Replace simulator placeholder throughout member
  • Template substitution: every '<AORAPPL>' is replaced with the configured application-owning region application name. Substitute application region name placeholder
  • Template substitution: every '<WSIMLGX>' is replaced with the name of the GenApp WSim log data set, written without quotes. Replace all placeholder tokens in member
  • Template substitution: every '<DB2HLQ>' is replaced with the configured database high-level qualifier. Substitute database qualifier placeholders in member
  • Template substitution: every '<KSDSPOL>' is replaced with the name of the policy load data set. Substitute policy dataset placeholder in member
  • Template substitution: every '<DBRMLIX>' is replaced with the name of the GenApp database request module library, written without quotes. Replace library placeholder with installation name
  • Template substitution: every '<CICSLIC>' is replaced with the configured name of the CICS licence data set. Substitute licence placeholder in member
  • Template substitution: every '<CSDNAME>' is replaced with the configured CICS system definition data set name. Replace CSD name placeholder
  • Template substitution: every '<WUIAPPL>' is replaced with the configured CICSPlex SM web user interface application name. Replace wui application placeholder
  • Template substitution: every '<MAPCOPX>' is replaced with the name of the GenApp map copybook library, written without quotes. Replace map copybook placeholder throughout member
  • Template substitution: every '<CMASAPPL>' is replaced with the configured CICSPlex SM address space (CMAS) application name. Substitute cmas application name placeholder
  • Template substitution: every '<DORSYSID>' is replaced with the data-owning region system identifier the installer set (shipped default 'DOR1'). As with every placeholder, build it as one entry in a placeholder-to-setting table read from the site configuration, and report a missing setting instead of leaving the placeholder in place. Substitute data region system identifier
12. Save customised installation members as copiesdraft · service · 3 requirements · 18 rules · 3 criteria

Saves each customised installation member as a separate copy, so installers can re-run the customisation at any time. The member ONCICS is saved as '#ONCICS', and every other member as '@' followed by its name. The shipped templates must never be changed, and each re-run replaces the earlier customised copy.

As an installer, I want each customised member saved as a separate copy while the original template stays unchanged, so that I can re-run the customisation and keep the shipped templates intact.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#12

Requirements

CodeClassRequirementCriteria
REQ-F-093design noteWhen the substitutions have been made in a member named 'ONCICS', the system shall save the whole customised text as a new member named '#ONCICS', replacing any existing member of that name.AC-01
REQ-F-094historical artifactWhen the substitutions have been made in a member with any name other than 'ONCICS', the system shall save the whole customised text as a member named '@' followed by the original member name, replacing any existing member of that name.AC-02
REQ-F-095design noteThe system shall leave the original template member unchanged, discarding the edit session after the customised copy has been saved under the prefixed name.AC-03

  • DEF-042 Is this intended? MAC1 fetches the log data set name (WSIMLOG) from the pool, but it replaces '<WSIMLOG>' with WSIMHLQ instead. Lines 41-46 do the same for '<PDSDBRM>', '<PDSMACP>', '<PDSLOAD>', '<PDSMSGS>' and '<WSIMSTL>'. This looks like a copy-and-paste slip. It does no harm today because no member uses these placeholders. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • When the template being customised is named 'ONCICS', its customised text is saved as a new output named '#ONCICS'. Derive prefixed backup member name
  • The whole customised text of 'ONCICS' is written as '#ONCICS' and overwrites any earlier output of that name, so the customisation can be re-run. Save full member content as copy
  • Every template other than 'ONCICS' is saved as a new output named '@' followed by the template name. Derive prefixed backup member name
  • The whole customised text of every other template is written under the '@'-prefixed name and overwrites any earlier output of that name, so the customisation can be re-run. Save full member content as copy
  • After '<LOADX>' has been replaced with the load library name, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace load library placeholder in member
  • After '<AORSYSID>' has been replaced with the application-owning region system identifier, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Substitute application-region system identifier placeholders
  • After '<DB2RUN>' has been replaced with the database run library value, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace run placeholder with configured value
  • After '<TORAPPL>' has been replaced with the terminal-owning region application identifier, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace tor application placeholder in member
  • After '<SOURCEX>' has been replaced with the source library name, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace source placeholder with environment name
  • After '<TORSYSID>' has been replaced with the terminal-owning region system identifier, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Substitute tor system identifier placeholders
  • After '<ZFSHOME>' has been replaced with the file-system home directory, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace home directory placeholders
  • After '<DB2DBID>' has been replaced with the database name, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace database id placeholders in member
  • After '<WSIMMSX>' has been replaced with the message-text library name, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Replace placeholder with session value
  • After '<DORAPPL>' has been replaced with the data-owning region application identifier, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Substitute data-owning region application name
  • After '<CICSHLQ>' has been replaced with the transaction-server library prefix, the result is saved only as the customised copy, never back into the template. Substitute transaction-server prefix placeholders
  • The shipped template is never modified. Substitutions are made on a working copy, which is discarded once the customised output has been saved under its prefixed name. Derive prefixed backup member name
  • After the customised copy is saved, the working edits are discarded, so the original template stays exactly as shipped and can be customised again. Save full member content as copy
13. Customise installation members with site valuesdraft · service · 5 requirements · 5 rules · 6 criteria · 2 gaps

Tailors the installation members to one site before the application is installed: every placeholder in each member is replaced with the value the installer set for that site, such as the Db2 subsystem, the CICSPlex SM address space and Web User Interface identifiers, and the Language Environment library qualifier. It serves the installer or platform team setting up an environment, so nobody has to edit members by hand. It must never leave a placeholder unreplaced, and never put a different setting's value in its place. One trap to keep: '<PDSLOAD>' gets the Workload Simulator qualifier, not the GenApp load library name.

As an installer, I want the installation customisation edit macro to replace the placeholders in each installation member with the values I set, so that the members are tailored to my site's subsystems and libraries without manual editing.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low. rec/Unassigned-Programs#13

Open questions

  • DEF-049 Is this intended? '<PDSLOAD>' is replaced with the Workload Simulator qualifier WSIMHLQ, not with the GenApp load library that CUST1 builds and passes (PDSLOAD, for example 'userid.GENAPP.LOAD'). This is part of the same pattern as the other PDS*/WSIM* placeholders in MAC1 lines 41-46. No shipped member uses the placeholder today. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • The CICSPlex SM Web User Interface system identifier becomes a per-environment deployment setting (default 'IWUI'). The deployment templating step fills every '<WUISYSID>' in the configuration and install templates with it. The step fails if the setting is missing, so no template is left with the placeholder. Replace wui system identifier placeholder
  • The Db2 subsystem identifier becomes a per-environment setting (default 'DKM1'), and the same templating step fills every '<DB2SSID>' with it. In the new application this is the database connection target in environment configuration. It must not be hard-coded in any member or in code. Substitute subsystem placeholder in member
  • The CICSPlex SM address space (CMAS) system identifier becomes a per-environment setting (default 'ICMA'). The templating step fills every '<CMASYSID>' with it. It is only needed while the target environment still runs CICSPlex SM; if the new platform has no CMAS, the setting and its placeholder can be dropped. Substitute cmas system identifier placeholder
  • The Language Environment runtime library qualifier becomes a per-environment setting (default 'CEE'). The templating step fills every '<CEEHLQ>' with it. On a non-mainframe runtime this maps to the location of the runtime libraries, or it is not needed at all. Replace runtime qualifier placeholders

Web Service Interface Generation

Web Service Interface Generation

1. Publish customer operations as web servicesdraft · scheduled job · 10 requirements · 10 rules · 12 criteria

Publishes the four customer operations (add customer, customer inquiry, customer update and customer number lookup) as callable web services, each at its own fixed address with a published service description, so that other applications can work with customers without going through the screens. It serves integration developers and the systems they connect. It must never publish a service whose request or response layout differs from the layout the customer program actually uses, and it must never move a service address (GENAPP/LGACUS01, GENAPP/LGICUS01, GENAPP/LGUCUS01, GENAPP/LGICVS01) that callers depend on.

As an integration developer, I want the customer add, customer inquiry, customer update and customer number programs published as web services with their binding files and service descriptions, so that other applications can call customer operations as web services.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches personal_data, updates_records. rec/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration#1
