Open questions

  • SME-107 When generating web service files fails (for example, a structure member is missing, the output directory can't be written, or the proxy can't be reached), what should happen: should the job fail, retry, or leave partial files behind? And when a job is run again, should it overwrite the existing binding, WSDL and log files or fail because they already exist? (Operations)
  • SME-108 The web service generation jobs use fixed settings from the legacy installation: Java directory java601_bit64_ga/J6.0.1_64, installation directory cics660, and HTTP proxy PROXY.HURSLEY.IBM.COM:80. Should the new system keep these values, replace them with equivalents, or make them configurable per environment? Is the proxy still needed at all? (Platform engineering)
  • SME-109 Output and log paths use the placeholders <ZFSHOME> and <SOURCEX>, and the source library is also a placeholder. What are the real base directory and source library in the target environment, and how should they be supplied to the new system? (Platform engineering)
  • SME-110 Once the binding file and service description have been generated, how are they deployed? Is deployment part of this business function or a separate process? (Integration team)
  • SME-113 Several generated binding files and WSDL files have no exact file names on record: add-policy Commercial, House and Endowment; inquiry House; customer update; update-policy Endowment and Commercial. Some recorded names also look irregular, such as 'HousePolicyWebServiceGenerationParameters' and 'WebServiceGenerationRequest.ws_bind'. What exact names must these files have for downstream consumers? Should they follow one convention, such as <service>.wsbind and <service>.wsdl? (Integration team)
  • SME-119 The customer update web service has an empty path prefix. Is that deliberate, or is it a placeholder that each environment should fill in? (Platform engineering)
  • SME-120 When the step that generates the web service definition (binding and WSDL) runs, what counts as success and what counts as failure? For example: what should happen if the request or response layout is invalid or incomplete, or if the output cannot be written, and may partial output be left behind after a failure? This applies to both the customer and the policy web service generation jobs. (Integration team)
  • SME-121 Where exactly should the new system read the source layouts from and write the generated web service files to? Today these locations are unfilled placeholders (<SOURCEX> and <ZFSHOME>). (Platform/infrastructure team)
  • SME-122 Environment settings used to generate the web services are currently fixed: the network proxy (PROXY.HURSLEY.IBM.COM:80), the Java runtime directory, the CICS install directory, and the source and output locations. Should these stay fixed or become configurable settings in the new system? (Platform operations team)
  • SME-123 The customer number web service takes a request (SOAVCII) and returns a response (SOAVCIO). What business information does each of these carry, that is, what does the published service actually expose to callers? (Business analyst)

Design notes

  • Expose add customer as an API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGACUS01. Its request and response contract comes from the one shared customer layout (SOAIC01), the same layout that inquiry and update use. Generate the contract from that layout so the two cannot drift apart. Generate customer add web service artifacts
  • Publish the add-customer service description, any runtime binding, and a generation log as build artifacts named after the service (LGACUS01). Put them where the deployment step and callers can find them under the installation home. Generation failures must show up in that log. Generate customer add web service artifacts
  • Expose customer inquiry as a read-only API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGICUS01. It uses the shared customer layout SOAIC01 for both request and response. Generate customer inquiry web service artifacts
  • Publish the customer inquiry service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGICUS01, in the same published-services and logs locations as the other customer services. Generate customer inquiry web service artifacts
  • Expose customer update as an API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGUCUS01, with the shared customer layout SOAIC01 for both request and response. The legacy generator reached the network through PROXY.HURSLEY.IBM.COM:80. Make the build's outbound proxy a configuration setting, not a fixed value. Generate customer update web service artifacts
  • Publish the customer update service description, binding and log as build artifacts named LGUCUS01. The legacy toolchain settings (Java 'java601_bit64_ga/J6.0.1_64', 'cics660', '/tmp', 'LS2WS') belong in build-environment configuration. They are not product behaviour. Generate customer update web service artifacts
  • Expose customer number lookup as an API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGICVS01. Unlike the other customer services, it has its own request layout (SOAVCII) and its own response layout (SOAVCIO), and the contract must keep those two shapes separate. Generate web service binding and WSDL
  • Publish the customer number service description, binding and log as build artifacts named LGICVS01. The toolchain directories and temp-file settings go in build configuration. Generate web service binding and WSDL
  • Contract generation for add customer runs as a repeatable build or pipeline step from the source layouts. The Java runtime, platform directory, temp location and HTTP proxy it needs become build-environment settings. Generate customer add web service artifacts
  • Contract generation for customer inquiry runs in the same repeatable build step as add customer, with the same configurable runtime, temp location and proxy settings. Generate customer inquiry web service artifacts
2. Publish policy add as web services by policy typedraft · scheduled job · 5 requirements · 4 rules · 4 criteria

Publishes adding a policy as four web services, one for each policy type (Motor, Endowment, House and Commercial). All four are served by the same policy add program, but each has its own address and its own policy-type layout. It serves integration developers whose systems create policies. It must never send a request to the wrong policy type's layout, and it must never change the addresses GENAPP/LGAPOLM1, GENAPP/LGAPOLE1, GENAPP/LGAPOLH1 and GENAPP/LGAPOLB1.

As an integration developer, I want the policy add program published as a separate web service for each policy type, so that other applications can add Motor, Endowment, House and Commercial policies as web services.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration#2

Design notes

  • Provide an add-Motor-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGAPOLM1. Its contract comes from the Motor policy layout SOAIPM1 and it routes to the shared policy add logic. Publish its service description, binding and log named LGAPOLM1. The outbound proxy is build configuration. Generate the Motor Policy add web service artifacts
  • Provide an add-Endowment-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGAPOLE1. Its contract comes from the Endowment layout SOAIPE1 and it routes to the shared policy add logic. Publish its artifacts named LGAPOLE1. Generate the endowment policy web service
  • Provide an add-House-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGAPOLH1. Its contract comes from the House layout SOAIPH1 and it routes to the shared policy add logic. Publish its artifacts named LGAPOLH1. The Java and platform directory settings are build-environment configuration. Generate the endowment policy web service
  • Provide an add-Commercial-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGAPOLB1. Its contract comes from the Commercial layout SOAIPB1 and it routes to the shared policy add logic. Publish its artifacts named LGAPOLB1. Toolchain settings are build configuration. Generate the endowment policy web service
3. Publish policy inquiry as web servicesdraft · scheduled job · 6 requirements · 6 rules · 6 criteria

Publishes policy lookup as web services: one inquiry service for each policy type (Motor, Commercial, House and Endowment), plus a mobile lookup that can return several policies in one response. It serves integration developers and mobile clients that need to read policies. It must never return a policy in a layout other than its type's layout, and it must keep the addresses GENAPP/LGIPOLM1, GENAPP/LGIPOLB1, GENAPP/LGIPOLH1, GENAPP/LGIPOLE1 and GENAPP/LGIPOL02 stable.

As an integration developer, I want the policy inquiry programs published as web services for each policy type and for mobile multiple-return lookup, so that other applications can look up policies as web services.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk low; touches reporting_only. rec/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration#3

Open questions

  • SME-107 When generating web service files fails (for example, a structure member is missing, the output directory can't be written, or the proxy can't be reached), what should happen: should the job fail, retry, or leave partial files behind? And when a job is run again, should it overwrite the existing binding, WSDL and log files or fail because they already exist? (Operations)
  • SME-113 Several generated binding files and WSDL files have no exact file names on record: add-policy Commercial, House and Endowment; inquiry House; customer update; update-policy Endowment and Commercial. Some recorded names also look irregular, such as 'HousePolicyWebServiceGenerationParameters' and 'WebServiceGenerationRequest.ws_bind'. What exact names must these files have for downstream consumers? Should they follow one convention, such as <service>.wsbind and <service>.wsdl? (Integration team)
  • SME-114 Some policy service variants don't state their runtime settings (Java directory, installation directory, path prefix, temporary directory and temporary file prefix): add-policy Endowment and Motor, the LGIPOLM1 and multiple-return inquiry variants, and update-policy House. Do they use the same settings as the other variants? (Platform engineering)
  • SME-116 The commercial, endowment, house and LGIPOLM1 policy inquiry services all point to the same program but use different request and response layouts. Is one program meant to serve all of these policy types, or is the program name a copy error in some of them? (Application architect)
  • SME-117 The multiple-return policy inquiry service (POLLOOK/POLLOO2, URI GENAPP/LGIPOL02) is grouped with house policy publication but calls a different program. Does it belong with the other policy inquiry services, and which policy type does it serve? (Application architect)
  • SME-118 One job triggers the policy inquiry services, but five service definitions are described. Which of them does that job actually generate, and in what order? (Operations)
  • DEF-050 Is this intended? The mobile step reuses the step name LS2WSB already used by the Commercial Policy step, so the job has two steps with the same name; both still run, but any reference to the step by name is ambiguous. (Subject-matter expert)

Design notes

  • Provide a read-only mobile policy lookup API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPOL02 that can return several policies in one response. Its request contract comes from POLLOOK and its response contract from POLLOO2. Publish its service description, binding and log named LGIPOL02. Generate the policy inquiry service binding and WSDL
  • Provide a read-only Motor policy inquiry API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPOLM1. Its request and response contract comes from the Motor layout SOAIPM1 and it routes to the shared policy inquiry logic. Publish its artifacts named LGIPOLM1. Generate the policy inquiry web service definition
  • Provide a read-only Commercial policy inquiry API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPOLB1. Its request and response contract comes from the Commercial layout SOAIPB1. Publish its artifacts named LGIPOLB1. Generate commercial policy inquiry web service
  • Provide a read-only House policy inquiry API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPOLH1. Its request and response contract comes from the House layout SOAIPH1. Publish its artifacts named LGIPOLH1. Generate House Policy inquiry web service
  • Provide a read-only Endowment policy inquiry API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPOLE1. Its request and response contract comes from the Endowment layout SOAIPE1. Publish its artifacts named LGIPOLE1. Generate endowment policy inquiry web service artifacts
  • Generate all five policy inquiry contracts in one repeatable build step. The runtime, platform directory, temp location and file-prefix settings it needs are shared build-environment configuration, not per-service code. Generate commercial policy inquiry web service
4. Publish policy update as web services by policy typedraft · scheduled job · 9 requirements · 8 rules · 8 criteria

Publishes updating a policy as four web services, one for each policy type (Motor, Commercial, Endowment and House). All four are served by the same policy update program, but each has its own address and its own policy-type layout. It serves integration developers whose systems change existing policies. It must never accept an update in another policy type's layout, and it must keep the addresses GENAPP/LGUPOLM1, GENAPP/LGUPOLB1, GENAPP/LGUPOLE1 and GENAPP/LGUPOLH1 stable.

As an integration developer, I want the policy update program published as a separate web service for each policy type, so that other applications can update Motor, Commercial, Endowment and House policies as web services.

Draft: the function is not signed off yet. Risk medium; touches updates_records. rec/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration/WebServiceInterfaceGeneration#4

Open questions

  • SME-111 The add-policy and update-policy web services each call one shared program for all four policy types (Commercial, Endowment, House, Motor), with a different request and response layout for each type. Should the new system keep one shared operation with four type-specific contracts, merge the contracts, or define a separate operation for each type? (Integration architect)
  • SME-112 The four policy-type web services for add-policy and for update-policy each have a single trigger, but each is documented as its own single-step job. Should the four be generated together in one job or as independent jobs, and if one fails, what should happen to the others? (Operations)
  • SME-113 Several generated binding files and WSDL files have no exact file names on record: add-policy Commercial, House and Endowment; inquiry House; customer update; update-policy Endowment and Commercial. Some recorded names also look irregular, such as 'HousePolicyWebServiceGenerationParameters' and 'WebServiceGenerationRequest.ws_bind'. What exact names must these files have for downstream consumers? Should they follow one convention, such as <service>.wsbind and <service>.wsdl? (Integration team)
  • SME-114 Some policy service variants don't state their runtime settings (Java directory, installation directory, path prefix, temporary directory and temporary file prefix): add-policy Endowment and Motor, the LGIPOLM1 and multiple-return inquiry variants, and update-policy House. Do they use the same settings as the other variants? (Platform engineering)

Design notes

  • Provide an update-Motor-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGUPOLM1. Its request and response contract comes from the Motor layout SOAIPM1 and it routes to the shared policy update logic. The outbound proxy is build configuration. Generate the policy update web service
  • Publish the Motor update service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGUPOLM1. The toolchain directories and temp settings go in build configuration. Generate the policy update web service
  • Provide an update-Commercial-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGUPOLB1. Its request and response contract comes from the Commercial layout SOAIPB1 and it routes to the shared policy update logic. Generate the policy update web service
  • Publish the Commercial update service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGUPOLB1. Toolchain settings are build configuration. Generate the policy update web service
  • Provide an update-Endowment-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGUPOLE1. Its request and response contract comes from the Endowment layout SOAIPE1 and it routes to the shared policy update logic. Generate the policy update web service
  • Publish the Endowment update service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGUPOLE1. Toolchain settings are build configuration. Generate the policy update web service
  • Provide an update-House-policy API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGUPOLH1. Its request and response contract comes from the House layout SOAIPH1 and it routes to the shared policy update logic. Define the house policy update service
  • Publish the House update service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGUPOLH1. Toolchain settings are build configuration. Define the house policy update service
5. Publish policy number lookup as a web servicedraft · scheduled job · 3 requirements · 2 rules · 3 criteria

Publishes policy number lookup as a single web service at the address GENAPP/LGIPVS01, so that other applications can look up policy numbers without the screens. It serves integration developers. It must never mix up its separate request and response layouts, and it must never move the service address that callers depend on.

As an integration developer, I want the policy number program published as a web service, so that other applications can call policy number lookup as a web service.

Open questions

  • SME-120 When the step that generates the web service definition (binding and WSDL) runs, what counts as success and what counts as failure? For example: what should happen if the request or response layout is invalid or incomplete, or if the output cannot be written, and may partial output be left behind after a failure? This applies to both the customer and the policy web service generation jobs. (Integration team)
  • SME-122 Environment settings used to generate the web services are currently fixed: the network proxy (PROXY.HURSLEY.IBM.COM:80), the Java runtime directory, the CICS install directory, and the source and output locations. Should these stay fixed or become configurable settings in the new system? (Platform operations team)
  • SME-124 Today request and response data are passed to the target program through a shared memory block (COMMAREA). What interface should the new service use to pass this data to the program that handles it? (Application architecture team)

Design notes

  • Provide a read-only policy number lookup API operation at the stable path GENAPP/LGIPVS01. It has its own request contract from SOAVPII and its own response contract from SOAVPIO. Both are generated from those layouts, and the outbound proxy is build configuration. Generate web service binding and WSDL
  • Publish the policy number service description, binding and generation log as build artifacts named LGIPVS01. The runtime directories and temp-file settings go in build-environment configuration. Generate web service binding and WSDL
